translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 116
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 116

sentences.zh: 【晉紀三十八】起重光大淵獻，盡閼逢攝提格，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 38] From Chongguang Dayuanxian through Quefeng Shetige; four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Records 38] From Chongguang Dayuanxian through Quefeng Shetige—four years in all.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝辛義熙七年（

translations.literal: Emperor An, Xin, seventh year of Yixi (
translations.idiomatic: The seventh year of Yixi of Emperor An (

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元四一一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, the year 411 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, 411 CE)

sentences.zh: 春正月己未，劉裕還建康。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, day jiwei, Liu Yu returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the jiwei day of the first month, Liu Yu returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 秦廣平公弼有寵於秦王興，為雍州刺史，鎮安定。

translations.literal: Qin Guangping Duke Bi had the favor of King Yao Xing of Qin; he was made Inspector of Yongzhou and garrisoned at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Guangping Duke Bi of Qin enjoyed the favor of King Yao Xing; he served as Inspector of Yongzhou and was stationed at Anding.

sentences.zh: 姜紀諂附於弼，勸弼結興左右以求入朝。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji flattered and attached himself to Bi, urging Bi to cultivate those close to Xing in order to seek entry to court.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji curried favor with Bi and urged him to win over those close to Yao Xing so that he might be summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 興征弼為尚書令、侍中、大將軍。

translations.literal: Xing summoned Bi as Director of the Masters of Writing, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing summoned Bi to serve as Director of the Masters of Writing, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 弼遂傾身結納朝士，收采名勢，以傾東宮；

translations.literal: Bi thereupon threw himself wholeheartedly into winning over court officials, gathering reputation and power to undermine the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Bi then devoted himself to cultivating ties with court officials and amassing influence and fame to undermine the crown prince;

sentences.zh: 國人惡之。

translations.literal: the people of the state hated him.
translations.idiomatic: and the people of the state came to detest him.

sentences.zh: 會興以西北多叛亂，欲命重將鎮撫之；

translations.literal: As it happened, because of many rebellions in the northwest, Xing wished to appoint a weighty general to pacify the region;
translations.idiomatic: When many rebellions broke out in the northwest, Yao Xing wished to appoint a powerful general to pacify the region;

sentences.zh: 隴東太守郭播請使弼出鎮，興不從，以太常索稜為太尉、領隴西內史，使招撫西秦。

translations.literal: Longdong Administrator Guo Bo requested that Bi be sent out to garrison; Xing did not agree, and instead made Grand Master of Ceremonies Suo Ling Grand Commandant and acting Interior Minister of Longxi, dispatching him to conciliate Western Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Longdong Administrator Guo Bo asked that Bi be sent out to take command; Yao Xing refused, instead making Grand Master of Ceremonies Suo Ling Grand Commandant and acting Interior Minister of Longxi to win over Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸遣使送所掠守宰，謝罪請降。

translations.literal: Western Qin King Qifu Gangui sent envoys to return the prefects and magistrates he had captured, apologizing and asking to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui, King of Western Qin, sent envoys to return the officials he had seized, apologizing and asking to submit.

sentences.zh: 興遣鴻臚拜乾歸都督隴西、嶺北、匈奴、雜胡諸軍事、征西大將軍、河州牧、單于、河南王，太子熾磐為鎮西將軍、左賢王、平昌公。

translations.literal: Xing sent the Director of Ceremonies to invest Gangui as Area Commander for Longxi, North of the Ridges, the Xiongnu, and the miscellaneous barbarians; General Who Conquers the West; Governor of Hezhou; Chanyu; and Prince of Henan; and his heir Chibpan as General Who Guards the West, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent the Director of Ceremonies to appoint Gangui Area Commander over military affairs in Longxi, north of the ranges, the Xiongnu, and various Hu peoples; General Who Conquers the West; Governor of Hezhou; Chanyu; and Prince of Henan; and his heir Chibpan as General Who Guards the West, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 興命群臣搜舉賢才。

translations.literal: Xing ordered the ministers to search out and recommend talented men.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing ordered his ministers to search out and recommend men of talent.

sentences.zh: 右僕射梁喜曰：「臣累受詔而未得其人，可謂世之乏才。」

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Liang Xi said, "This subject has repeatedly received the edict yet not obtained such men—one may say the age lacks talent."
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Liang Xi said, "I have repeatedly received Your Majesty's edict yet found no such men—it would seem the age lacks talent."

sentences.zh: 興曰：「自古帝王之興，未嘗取相於昔人。

translations.literal: Xing said, "Since antiquity the rise of emperors and kings has never taken their chancellors from former men.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing said, "Since antiquity, when emperors and kings rose to power, they never chose their chancellors from men of the past.

sentences.zh: 待將於將來，隨時任才，皆能致治。

translations.literal: They wait on generals yet to come; according to the times they employ talent, and all can bring order.
translations.idiomatic: They wait for leaders yet to come and appoint talent according to the times—each age can achieve good government.

sentences.zh: 卿自識拔不明，豈得遠誣四海乎！」

translations.literal: You yourself do not discern and elevate clearly—how can you falsely blame the realm within the four seas!"
translations.idiomatic: Your own judgment in recognizing and promoting men is unclear—how can you falsely blame the whole realm!"

sentences.zh: 群臣咸悅。

translations.literal: The ministers were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were all pleased.

sentences.zh: 秦姚詳屯杏城，為夏王勃勃所逼，南奔大蘇；

translations.literal: Qin Yao Xiang was encamped at Xingcheng, pressed by Xia King Heluobobo, and fled south to Dasu;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang of Qin was encamped at Xingcheng but was driven by Xia King Heluobobo to flee south to Dasu;

sentences.zh: 勃勃遣平東將軍鹿弈干追斬之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Bobobo sent General Who Pacifies the East Lu Yigan in pursuit to behead him and captured all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Heluobobo sent General Who Pacifies the East Lu Yigan in pursuit to kill him and took all his troops captive.

sentences.zh: 勃勃南攻安定，破尚書楊佛嵩於青石北原，降其眾四萬五千；

translations.literal: Bobobo attacked south toward Anding, defeated Master of Writing Yang Fosong at the north plain of Qing Stone, and received the surrender of forty-five thousand of his men;
translations.idiomatic: Heluobobo marched south against Anding, defeated Master of Writing Yang Fosong on the north plain of Qing Stone, and accepted the surrender of forty-five thousand men;

sentences.zh: 進攻東鄉，下之，徙三千餘戶於貳城。

translations.literal: he advanced to attack Dongxiang, took it, and moved more than three thousand households to Ercheng.
translations.idiomatic: then advanced on Dongxiang, captured it, and relocated more than three thousand households to Ercheng.

sentences.zh: 秦鎮北參軍王買德奔夏，夏王勃勃問以滅秦之策，買德曰：「秦德雖衰，籓鎮猶固，願且蓄力以待之。」

translations.literal: Qin Northern Garrison Army Aide Wang Maide fled to Xia; Xia King Heluobobo asked him for a strategy to destroy Qin; Maide said, "Though Qin's virtue has declined, its frontier commands remain firm; I wish to store up strength for the time being and wait."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maide, an aide in the Northern Garrison Army of Qin, defected to Xia; Heluobobo asked him how Qin might be destroyed. Maide said, "Though Qin's power has waned, its frontier commands remain strong; we should gather our strength and wait."

sentences.zh: 勃勃以買德為軍師中郎將。

translations.literal: Bobobo made Maide Army Adviser Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Heluobobo appointed Maide Army Adviser Commandant.

sentences.zh: 秦王興遣衛大將軍常山公顯迎姚詳，弗及，遂屯杏城。

translations.literal: King Yao Xing of Qin sent Guard General Changshan Duke Xian to welcome Yao Xiang but did not reach him in time, and so encamped at Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: King Yao Xing of Qin sent Guard General Changshan Duke Xian to welcome Yao Xiang but arrived too late, and encamped at Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 劉籓帥孟懷玉等諸將追盧循至嶺表。

translations.literal: Liu Fan led the generals Meng Huaiyu and others in pursuit of Lu Xun to the region south of the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan led Generals Meng Huaiyu and others in pursuit of Lu Xun beyond the Ling ranges.

sentences.zh: 二月壬午，懷玉克始興，斬徐道覆。

translations.literal: In the second month, day renwu, Huaiyu captured Shixing and beheaded Xu Daofu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the renwu day, Meng Huaiyu took Shixing and beheaded Xu Daofu.

sentences.zh: 河南王乾歸徙鮮卑僕渾部三千餘戶於度堅城，以子敕勃為秦興太守以鎮之。

translations.literal: Prince of Henan Qifu Gangui moved more than three thousand households of the Xianbei Puhun tribe to Dujian City and made his son Chibo Governor of Qinxing to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui, Prince of Henan, relocated more than three thousand households of the Xianbei Puhun tribe to Dujian City and appointed his son Chibo Governor of Qinxing to guard the place.

sentences.zh: 焦朗猶據姑臧，沮渠蒙遜攻拔其城，執朗而宥之；

translations.literal: Jiao Lang still held Guzang; Juqu Mengxun attacked and took the city, seized Lang, and pardoned him;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Lang still held Guzang; Juqu Mengxun stormed the city, seized Lang, and spared his life;

sentences.zh: 以其弟挐為秦州刺史，鎮姑臧。

translations.literal: he made Lang's younger brother Ju Governor of Qinzhou and garrisoned Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Lang's younger brother Ju Governor of Qinzhou to garrison Guzang.

sentences.zh: 遂伐南涼，圍樂都。

translations.literal: He then attacked Southern Liang and besieged Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched against Southern Liang and besieged Ledu.

sentences.zh: 三旬不克；

translations.literal: After thirty days he did not take it;
translations.idiomatic: After thirty days he had not taken it;

sentences.zh: 南涼王辱檀以子安周為質，乃還。

translations.literal: Southern Liang King Tufa Rutan gave his son Anzhou as hostage, and Mengxun then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Rutan, King of Southern Liang, offered his son Anzhou as a hostage, and Mengxun then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾樹洛干伐南涼，敗南涼太子虎台。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun Shulogan attacked Southern Liang and defeated Southern Liang Crown Prince Hutai.
translations.idiomatic: Shulogan of Tuyuhun attacked Southern Liang and defeated Crown Prince Hutai of Southern Liang.

sentences.zh: 南涼王辱檀欲復伐沮渠蒙遜，邯川護軍孟愷諫曰：「蒙遜新並姑臧，凶勢方盛，不可攻也。」

translations.literal: Southern Liang King Tufa Rutan wished again to attack Juqu Mengxun; Hanchuan Protector of the Army Meng Kai remonstrated, saying, "Mengxun has newly annexed Guzang; his fierce momentum is at its height—it cannot be attacked."
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Rutan, King of Southern Liang, wished to attack Juqu Mengxun again; Hanchuan Protector of the Army Meng Kai remonstrated, saying, "Mengxun has only just taken Guzang; his power is at its height—we must not attack him."

sentences.zh: 辱檀不從，五道俱進，至番禾、苕藋，掠五千餘戶而還。

translations.literal: Rutan did not listen, advanced by five routes together, reached Fanchang and Tiaodiao, plundered more than five thousand households, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan would not heed him, advanced along five routes to Fanchang and Tiaodiao, plundered more than five thousand households, and returned.

sentences.zh: 將軍屈右曰：「今既獲利，宜倍道旋師，早度險困。

translations.literal: General Qu You said, "Now that we have gained profit, we should double our marching speed and turn the army back, crossing the dangerous passes early.
translations.idiomatic: General Qu You said, "We have already gained our spoils; we should march at double speed and withdraw while we can still cross the difficult passes.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜善用兵，若輕軍猝至，大敵外逼，徙戶內叛，此危道也。」

translations.literal: Mengxun is skilled in using troops; if a light force suddenly arrives, a great enemy presses from outside, and the relocated households rebel within, this is a perilous course."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun is skilled in war; if a light force suddenly appears, a great enemy closes in from without, and the relocated households rebel within, we will be in grave danger."

sentences.zh: 衛尉伊力延曰：「彼步我騎，勢不相及。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guards Yiliyan said, "They are infantry and we are cavalry; our momentum cannot be matched.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Guards Yiliyan said, "They march on foot and we ride; they cannot catch us.

sentences.zh: 今倍道而歸則示弱，且捐棄資財，非計也。」

translations.literal: If we now return at double speed we show weakness, and moreover we abandon goods and wealth—this is no plan."
translations.idiomatic: To withdraw at double speed now would show weakness and mean abandoning our spoils—it is no strategy."

sentences.zh: 俄而昏霧風雨，蒙遜兵大至，辱檀敗走。

translations.literal: Before long, dusk mist and wind and rain came; Mengxun's troops arrived in force, and Rutan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon dusk brought mist, wind, and rain; Mengxun's army arrived in force, and Rutan was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜進圍樂都，辱檀嬰城固守，以子染干為質以請和，蒙遜乃還。

translations.literal: Mengxun advanced to besiege Ledu; Rutan tied himself to the city and held firm, giving his son Ranggan as hostage to seek peace, and Mengxun then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun advanced to besiege Ledu; Rutan held the city and resisted, offering his son Ranggan as a hostage to sue for peace, and Mengxun then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三月，劉裕始受太尉、中書監，以劉穆之為太尉司馬，陳郡殷景仁為行參軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, Liu Yu first received the posts of Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; he made Liu Muzhi Grand Commandant Major and Chen Commandery Yin Jingren Acting Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Liu Yu first accepted the posts of Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; he appointed Liu Muzhi Grand Commandant Major and Yin Jingren of Chen Commandery Acting Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 裕問穆之曰：「孟昶參佐誰堪入我府者？」

translations.literal: Yu asked Muzhi, "Among Meng Chang's aides, who is fit to enter my headquarters?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked Muzhi, "Among Meng Chang's aides, who is fit to join my staff?"

sentences.zh: 穆之舉前建威中兵參軍謝晦。

translations.literal: Muzhi recommended former Jianwei Central Army Aide Xie Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi recommended the former Jianwei Central Army Aide Xie Hui.

sentences.zh: 晦，安兄據之曾孫也，裕即命為參軍。

translations.literal: Hui was the great-grandson of Xie An's elder brother Ju; Yu immediately appointed him Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was the great-grandson of Xie An's elder brother Ju; Yu immediately appointed him Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 裕嘗訊囚，其旦，刑獄參軍有疾，以晦代之；

translations.literal: Yu once interrogated prisoners; that morning the Prisons Army Aide was ill, and Hui replaced him;
translations.idiomatic: Once when Yu was interrogating prisoners, the Prisons Army Aide fell ill that morning and Hui took his place;

sentences.zh: 於車中一覽訊牒，催促便下。

translations.literal: in the carriage he glanced once through the interrogation documents, urged haste, and the cases were concluded.
translations.idiomatic: in the carriage he read through the case files at a glance, pressed for speed, and the judgments were handed down.

sentences.zh: 相府多事，獄系殷積，晦隨問酬辨，曾無違謬；

translations.literal: The chancellor's office had many affairs; prisoners in the jails piled up thickly; Hui answered as each was questioned, never once erring;
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's office was overwhelmed with business and the jails were crowded; Hui answered each case as it came, never once erring;

sentences.zh: 裕由是奇之，即日署刑獄賊曹。

translations.literal: Yu therefore marveled at him and that same day appointed him to the Prisons and Banditry Section.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was struck by this and that same day appointed him to the Prisons and Banditry Section.

sentences.zh: 晦美風姿，善言笑，博贍多通，裕深加賞愛。

translations.literal: Hui had fine bearing, was skilled in speech and laughter, was broadly learned and widely versed, and Yu deeply prized and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was handsome and graceful, witty in conversation, broadly learned and accomplished in many fields, and Yu came to value him deeply.

sentences.zh: 盧循行收兵至番禺，遂圍之。

translations.literal: Lu Xun, while gathering troops on the march, reached Panyu and thereupon besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun, gathering troops as he marched, reached Panyu and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 孫處據守二十餘日。

translations.literal: Sun Chu held the defense for more than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu held the city for more than twenty days.

sentences.zh: 沈田子言於劉籓曰：「番禺城雖險固。

translations.literal: Shen Tianzi said to Liu Fan, "Though Panyu city is perilous and firm.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tianzi said to Liu Fan, "Though Panyu is strong and well fortified,

sentences.zh: 本賊之巢穴；

translations.literal: it is originally the rebels' lair;
translations.idiomatic: it is the rebels' own stronghold;

sentences.zh: 今循圍之，或有內變。

translations.literal: now that Xun besieges it, there may be internal mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: and now that Xun besieges it, there may be unrest within the walls.

sentences.zh: 且孫季高眾力寡弱，不能持久，若使賊還據廣州，凶勢復振矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover Sun Jigao's forces are few and weak and cannot endure long; if the bandits return to hold Guangzhou, their fierce momentum will revive."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Sun Jigao's force is small and cannot hold out long; if the rebels regain Guangzhou, their power will rise again."

sentences.zh: 夏四月，田子引兵救番禺，擊循，破之，所殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Tianzi led troops to relieve Panyu, attacked Xun, defeated him, and killed more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Tianzi led troops to relieve Panyu, attacked Xun, defeated him, and killed more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 循走，田子與處共追之，又破循於危梧、鬱林、寧浦。

translations.literal: Xun fled; Tianzi and Chu together pursued him and again defeated Xun at Weiwo, Yulin, and Ningpu.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fled; Tianzi and Chu pursued him together and again defeated him at Weiwo, Yulin, and Ningpu.

sentences.zh: 會處病，不能進，循奔交州。

translations.literal: As it happened Chu fell ill and could not advance; Xun fled to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chu then fell ill and could advance no farther; Xun fled toward Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，九真太守李遜作亂，交州刺史交趾杜瑗討斬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiuzhen Administrator Li Xun had raised a rebellion; Jiaozhou Inspector Du Yuan of Jiaozhi campaigned against and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Xun, Administrator of Jiuzhen, had rebelled; Du Yuan of Jiaozhi, Inspector of Jiaozhou, campaigned against him and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 瑗卒，朝廷以其子慧度為交州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan died; the court made his son Huidu Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan died, the court appointed his son Huidu Inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 詔書未至，循襲破合浦，逕向交州；

translations.literal: Before the imperial edict arrived, Xun raided and took Hepu and went straight toward Jiaozhou;
translations.idiomatic: Before the imperial edict arrived, Xun raided Hepu and marched straight on Jiaozhou;

sentences.zh: 慧度帥州府文武拒循於石碕，破之，循餘眾猶三千人，李遜餘黨李脫等結集俚獠五千餘人以應循。

translations.literal: Huidu led the civil and military officials of the province and prefecture to resist Xun at Shiji, defeated him; Xun's remaining followers were still three thousand; Li Xun's remnant partisans Li Tuo and others gathered more than five thousand Li and Liao to respond to Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu led the officials and troops of the province to resist Xun at Shiji and defeated him; Xun still had three thousand men left, and Li Tuo and other remnant followers of Li Xun rallied more than five thousand Li and Liao peoples to join him.

sentences.zh: 庚子，循晨至龍編南津；

translations.literal: On gengzi, at dawn Xun reached the southern ford of Longbian;
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day, at dawn Xun reached the southern ford of Longbian;

sentences.zh: 慧度悉散家財以賞軍士，與循合戰，擲雉尾炬焚其艦，以步兵夾岸射之，循從艦俱然，兵眾大潰。

translations.literal: Huidu distributed all his family wealth to reward the soldiers, joined battle with Xun, hurled pheasant-tail torches to burn his ships, and had infantry on both banks shoot; Xun's attendants and ships all burned together, and the army masses collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu distributed all his family wealth to reward his troops, joined battle with Xun, hurled pheasant-tail torches to set his ships ablaze, and had infantry on both banks shoot; Xun's ships and followers burned together, and his army broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 循知不免，先鴆妻子，召妓妾問曰：「誰能從我死者？」

translations.literal: Xun knew he could not escape; he first poisoned his wife and children, summoned his singing girls and concubines and asked, "Who can die with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, Xun first poisoned his wife and children, then summoned his concubines and asked, "Who will die with me?"

sentences.zh: 多雲；

translations.literal: Many clouded over;
translations.idiomatic: Many fell silent;

sentences.zh: 「雀鼠貪生，就死實難。」

translations.literal: "Sparrows and mice crave life; to approach death is truly hard."
translations.idiomatic: saying, "Sparrows and mice cling to life; death is hard to face."

sentences.zh: 或云：「官尚當死，某豈願生！」

translations.literal: Some said, "Your lordship is still to die—how could I wish to live!"
translations.idiomatic: Others said, "My lord is about to die—how could I wish to live!"

sentences.zh: 乃悉殺諸辭死者，因自投於水。

translations.literal: He then killed all who had declined death, and thereupon threw himself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed all who had refused, and threw himself into the water.

sentences.zh: 慧度取其屍斬之，並其父子及李脫等，函七首送建康。

translations.literal: Huidu took his corpse and beheaded it, together with his father and sons and Li Tuo and others, placed seven heads in a box, and sent them to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu took his corpse and beheaded it, together with his father, sons, Li Tuo, and the rest; he placed seven heads in a box and sent them to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 初，劉毅在京口，貧困，與知識射於東堂。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Yi was at Jingkou, poor and in want, and shot with acquaintances in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Yi was at Jingkou in poverty, he would shoot with acquaintances in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 庾悅為司徒右長史，後至，奪其射堂；

translations.literal: Yu Yue was Chief Clerk of the Right to the Minister of Education; arriving later, he seized the shooting hall;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue was Chief Clerk of the Right to the Minister of Education; arriving later, he took over the shooting hall;

sentences.zh: 眾人皆避之，毅獨不去。

translations.literal: everyone else yielded; Yi alone did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: everyone else yielded, but Yi alone did not budge.

sentences.zh: 悅廚饌甚盛，不以及毅；

translations.literal: Yue's kitchen fare was very lavish, but he did not extend it to Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Yue's table was lavish, but he did not share with Yi;

sentences.zh: 毅從悅求子鵝炙，悅怒不與，毅由是銜之。

translations.literal: Yi asked Yue for roast cygnet; Yue angrily would not give it, and Yi thereby bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked Yue for roast cygnet; Yue angrily refused, and Yi bore a grudge from that day.

sentences.zh: 至是，毅求兼督江州，詔許之，因奏稱：「江州內地，以治民為職。

translations.literal: At this time Yi requested concurrent supervision of Jiangzhou; the edict permitted it, and he memorialized, saying, "Jiangzhou is interior territory; its duty is to govern the people.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yi requested concurrent supervision of Jiangzhou; the edict granted it, and he memorialized, saying, "Jiangzhou is interior territory, and its duty is to govern the people.

sentences.zh: 不當置軍府凋耗民力，宜罷軍府移鎮豫章；

translations.literal: It is not fitting to set up a military headquarters that drains and wastes the people's strength; the military headquarters should be abolished and the garrison moved to Yuzhang;
translations.idiomatic: It is not fitting to maintain a military headquarters that drains the people's strength; the headquarters should be abolished and the garrison moved to Yuzhang;

sentences.zh: 而尋陽接蠻，可即州府千兵以助郡戍。」

translations.literal: whereas Xunyang borders the barbarians, and a thousand troops from the provincial headquarters may immediately assist the commandery garrison."
translations.idiomatic: whereas Xunyang borders the barbarians and may be garrisoned with a thousand troops from the provincial headquarters to assist the commandery defense."

sentences.zh: 於是解悅都督、將軍官，以刺史鎮豫章。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue was relieved of his posts as area commander and general; as inspector he was stationed at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was thereupon stripped of his posts as area commander and general and, as inspector, was stationed at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 毅以親將趙恢領千兵守尋陽；

translations.literal: Yi made his close general Zhao Hui lead a thousand troops to guard Xunyang;
translations.idiomatic: Yi placed his close general Zhao Hui in command of a thousand troops at Xunyang;

sentences.zh: 悅府文武三千悉入毅府，符攝嚴峻。

translations.literal: all three thousand civil and military officials of Yue's headquarters entered Yi's headquarters; the orders and summonses were severe and strict.
translations.idiomatic: and all three thousand civil and military officials of Yue's headquarters were transferred to Yi's command under stern orders.

sentences.zh: 悅忿懼，至豫章，疽發背卒。

translations.literal: Yue, resentful and afraid, reached Yuzhang; a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue, furious and afraid, reached Yuzhang, where a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.

sentences.zh: 河南王乾歸徙羌句豈等部眾五千餘戶於疊蘭城，以兄子阿柴為興國太守以鎮之。

translations.literal: Prince of Henan Qifu Gangui moved more than five thousand households of the Qiang tribes Juqi and others to Dielan City and made his elder brother's son Achai Governor of Xingguo to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui, Prince of Henan, relocated more than five thousand households of the Qiang tribes led by Juqi and others to Dielan City and appointed his nephew Achai Governor of Xingguo to guard the place.

sentences.zh: 五月，復以子木欒干為武威太守，鎮□□良城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, he again made his son Mulanggan Governor of Wuwei, garrisoning the city of [lacuna]liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, he again appointed his son Mulanggan Governor of Wuwei to garrison the city of [lacuna]liang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，魏主嗣謁金陵，山陽候奚斤居守。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Wei ruler Si paid respects at Jinling; Shanyang Marquis Xi Jin remained to guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day, Emperor Si of Wei paid his respects at Jinling, while Shanyang Marquis Xi Jin remained behind as guardian.

sentences.zh: 昌黎王慕容伯兒謀反；

translations.literal: Changli King Murong Bo'er plotted rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Changli King Murong Bo'er plotted rebellion;

sentences.zh: 己已，奚斤並其黨收斬之。

translations.literal: On jisi, Xi Jin seized him together with his partisans and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day, Xi Jin seized him and his followers and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，燕王跋以太子永領大單于，置四輔。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Yan King Ba made Crown Prince Yong Grand Chanyu and established four assistants.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, King Ba of Yan made Crown Prince Yong Grand Chanyu and established four assistants.

sentences.zh: 柔然可汗斛律遣使獻馬三千匹於跋，求娶跋女樂浪公主。

translations.literal: Rouran Khagan Hulu sent envoys to present three thousand horses to Ba and sought to marry Ba's daughter Princess Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu, Khagan of the Rouran, sent envoys to present three thousand horses to Ba and asked for the hand of Ba's daughter, Princess Lelang.

sentences.zh: 跋命群臣議之。

translations.literal: Ba ordered the ministers to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: Ba ordered his ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 遼西公素弗曰：「前世皆以宗女妻六夷，宜許以妃嬪之女，樂浪公主不宜下降非類。」

translations.literal: Liaoxi Duke Sufu said, "Former ages all married clan daughters to the Six Barbarians; one should consent to give a daughter of a consort, but Princess Lelang ought not descend to marry a non-kind."
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi Duke Sufu said, "Former ages married imperial clan daughters to the Six Barbarians; we should offer a daughter of a consort, but Princess Lelang ought not be given to a foreign people."

sentences.zh: 跋曰：「朕方崇信殊俗，奈何欺之！」

translations.literal: Ba said, "I am just now honoring and trusting foreign customs—how can I deceive them!"
translations.idiomatic: Ba said, "I mean to honor and trust foreign peoples—how can I deceive them!"

sentences.zh: 乃以樂浪公主妻之。

translations.literal: He then gave Princess Lelang in marriage to him.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Princess Lelang to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 跋勤於政事，勸課農桑，省徭役，薄賦斂；

translations.literal: Ba was diligent in government affairs, urged agricultural mulberry work, reduced corvée labor, and lightened taxes and levies;
translations.idiomatic: Ba was diligent in government, encouraged farming and sericulture, reduced corvée labor, and lightened taxes;

sentences.zh: 每遣守宰，必親引見，問為政之要，以觀其能。

translations.literal: whenever he dispatched prefects and magistrates, he always personally summoned them for audience, asked the essentials of governing, and thereby observed their ability.
translations.idiomatic: whenever he appointed prefects and magistrates, he personally received them, asked the essentials of good government, and judged their ability thereby.

sentences.zh: 燕人悅之。

translations.literal: The people of Yan were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yan were pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 河南王乾歸遣平昌公熾磐及中軍將軍審虔伐南涼。

translations.literal: Prince of Henan Qifu Gangui sent Pingchang Duke Chibpan and Central Army General Shen Qian to attack Southern Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui, Prince of Henan, sent Pingchang Duke Chibpan and Central Army General Shen Qian against Southern Liang.

sentences.zh: 審虔，乾歸之子也。

translations.literal: Shen Qian was Gangui's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qian was Gangui's son.

sentences.zh: 八月，熾磐兵濟河，南涼王辱檀遣太子虎台逆戰於嶺南。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Chibpan's troops crossed the river; Southern Liang King Tufa Rutan sent Crown Prince Hutai to meet them in battle south of the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Chibpan's army crossed the river; Tufa Rutan sent Crown Prince Hutai to meet them in battle south of the ranges.

sentences.zh: 南涼兵敗，虜牛馬十餘萬而還。

translations.literal: Southern Liang's army was defeated; they captured more than a hundred thousand cattle and horses and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Liang was defeated; Chibpan seized more than a hundred thousand head of cattle and horses and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜帥輕騎襲西涼，西涼公暠曰：「兵有不戰而敗敵者，挫其銳也。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun led light cavalry in a raid on Western Liang; Western Liang Duke Li Gao said, "In warfare there is defeating the enemy without fighting—by blunting his sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun led light cavalry in a surprise attack on Western Liang; Li Gao, Duke of Western Liang, said, "Sometimes one defeats an enemy without fighting—by blunting his momentum.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜新與吾盟，而遽來襲我，我閉門不與戰，待其銳氣竭而擊之，蔑不克矣。」

translations.literal: Mengxun has newly allied with us yet suddenly comes to raid us; I shall shut the gates and not give battle, wait until his sharp momentum is exhausted and then strike—nothing will fail to be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun has only just made alliance with us, yet he comes to attack at once; I shall shut the gates and refuse battle until his momentum fades, then strike—we cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 頃之，蒙遜糧盡而歸，暠遣世子歆帥騎七邀擊之，蒙遜大敗，獲其將沮渠百年。

translations.literal: Before long Mengxun's grain was exhausted and he withdrew; Gao sent his heir Xin at the head of seven thousand cavalry to intercept him; Mengxun was greatly defeated, and they captured his general Juqu Bainian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mengxun ran out of supplies and withdrew; Gao sent his heir Xin with seven thousand cavalry to intercept him; Mengxun suffered a crushing defeat, and they captured his general Juqu Bainian.

sentences.zh: 河南王乾歸攻秦略陽太守姚在於柏陽堡，克之。

translations.literal: Prince of Henan Qifu Gangui attacked Qin Lueyang Administrator Yao Zai at Boyang Fort and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui attacked Yao Zai, Administrator of Lueyang in Qin, at Boyang Fort and took it.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，進攻南平太守王憬於水洛城，又克之，徙民三千餘戶於譚郊。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, he advanced to attack Nanping Administrator Wang Jing at Shuilo City, again took it, and moved more than three thousand households to Tanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, he attacked Nanping Administrator Wang Jing at Shuilo City, took it, and relocated more than three thousand households to Tanjiao.

sentences.zh: 遣乞伏審虔帥眾二萬城譚郊。

translations.literal: He dispatched Qifu Shen Qian to lead twenty thousand men to fortify Tanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qifu Shen Qian with twenty thousand men to fortify Tanjiao.

sentences.zh: 十二月，西羌彭利發襲據枹罕，自稱大將軍、河州牧，乾歸討之，不克。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Western Qiang Peng Lifa raided and seized Fuhan, styled himself Grand General and Governor of Hezhou; Gangui campaigned against him but did not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Peng Lifa of the Western Qiang seized Fuhan and styled himself Grand General and Governor of Hezhou; Gangui attacked him but could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，并州刺史劉道憐為北徐刺史，移鎮彭城。

translations.literal: That year, Bingzhou Inspector Liu Daolian was made Inspector of Northern Xu and moved his garrison to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Liu Daolian, Inspector of Bingzhou, was appointed Inspector of Northern Xu and moved his headquarters to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝辛義熙八年（

translations.literal: Emperor An, Xin, eighth year of Yixi (
translations.idiomatic: The eighth year of Yixi of Emperor An (

sentences.zh: 壬子，公元四一二年）

translations.literal: renzi, the year 412 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renzi, 412 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，河南王乾歸復討彭利發，至奴葵谷，利發棄眾南走，乾歸遣振威將軍乞伏公府追至清水，斬之，收羌戶一萬三千，以乞伏審虔為河州刺史鎮枹罕而還。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Prince of Henan Qifu Gangui again campaigned against Peng Lifa; reaching Nukui Valley, Lifa abandoned his followers and fled south; Gangui sent General Who Quells Might Qifu Gongfu in pursuit to Qingshui, beheaded him, gathered thirteen thousand Qiang households, made Qifu Shen Qian Inspector of Hezhou to garrison Fuhan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Qifu Gangui again campaigned against Peng Lifa; reaching Nukui Valley, Lifa abandoned his troops and fled south; Gangui sent General Who Quells Might Qifu Gongfu in pursuit to Qingshui, killed him, gathered thirteen thousand Qiang households, appointed Qifu Shen Qian Inspector of Hezhou to garrison Fuhan, and returned.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙子，以吳興太守孔靖為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingzi, Wu Xing Administrator Kong Jing was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the bingzi day, Kong Jing, Administrator of Wu Xing, was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 河南王乾歸徙都譚郊，命平昌公熾磐鎮苑川。

translations.literal: Prince of Henan Qifu Gangui moved his capital to Tanjiao and ordered Pingchang Duke Chibpan to garrison Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui moved his capital to Tanjiao and ordered Pingchang Duke Chibpan to garrison Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 乾歸擊吐谷渾阿若干於赤水，降之。

translations.literal: Gangui attacked Tuyuhun Aogan at Chishui and received his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui attacked Aogan of Tuyuhun at Chishui and accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，劉道規以疾求歸，許之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Liu Daogui requested to return on account of illness, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Liu Daogui asked to return home because of illness, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 道規在荊州累年，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: Daogui had been in Jingzhou for many years without the slightest offense.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui had governed Jingzhou for many years without the slightest abuse of power.

sentences.zh: 及歸，府庫帷幕，儼然若舊。

translations.literal: When he returned, the storehouses, curtains, and hangings were as if unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed, the storehouses and furnishings were exactly as he had found them.

sentences.zh: 隨身甲士二人遷席於舟中，道規刑之於市。

translations.literal: Two armored attendants who had moved his seat aboard the boat were punished by Daogui in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Two armored attendants who had moved his seat aboard the boat were executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 以後將軍豫州刺史劉毅為衛將軍、都督荊、寧、秦、雍四州諸軍事、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Rear General and Inspector of Yuzhou Liu Yi was made Guard General, Area Commander for military affairs in Jing, Ning, Qin, and Yong provinces, and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, Rear General and Inspector of Yuzhou, was appointed Guard General, Area Commander over military affairs in Jing, Ning, Qin, and Yong provinces, and Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 毅謂左衛將軍劉敬宣曰：「吾忝西任，欲屈卿為長史南蠻，豈有見輔意乎？」

translations.literal: Yi said to Left Guard General Liu Jingxuan, "I am unworthy of the western appointment and wish to humble you as Chief Clerk of the Southern Barbarians—would you have the will to assist me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said to Left Guard General Liu Jingxuan, "I am honored with this western command and wish to appoint you Chief Clerk of the Southern Barbarians—would you be willing to assist me?"

sentences.zh: 敬宣懼，以告太尉裕。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was afraid and told Grand Commandant Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan was alarmed and reported this to Grand Commandant Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕笑曰：「但令老兄平安，必無過慮。」

translations.literal: Yu smiled and said, "So long as my elder brother is safe, there will certainly be no excessive worry."
translations.idiomatic: Yu smiled and said, "So long as my elder brother is safe, you need not worry excessively."

sentences.zh: 毅性剛愎，自謂建義之功與裕相埒，深自矜伐，雖權事推裕而心不服。

translations.literal: Yi was by nature stubborn and self-willed; he considered his merit in founding the cause equal to Yu's, deeply prided himself and boasted; though in matters of power he deferred to Yu, in his heart he did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was stubborn and headstrong; he believed his merit in founding the regime equaled Yu's and was deeply proud of himself; though he deferred to Yu in public affairs, in his heart he would not submit.

sentences.zh: 及居方岳，常怏怏不得志。

translations.literal: When he held a frontier command, he was constantly discontented and unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held a frontier command, he was constantly dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 裕每柔而順之，毅驕縱滋甚，嘗云：「恨不遇劉、項，與之爭中原！」

translations.literal: Yu always treated him gently and yielded to him; Yi's arrogance and license grew ever greater; he once said, "I regret not meeting Liu Bang and Xiang Yu—to contend with them for the Central Plains!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu always treated him gently, but Yi's arrogance only grew; he once said, "I regret that I did not live in the age of Liu Bang and Xiang Yu—I would have contended with them for the Central Plains!"

sentences.zh: 及敗於桑落，知物情已去，彌復憤激。

translations.literal: When he was defeated at Sangluo, knowing that popular sentiment had already left him, he became all the more resentful and agitated.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat at Sangluo, knowing that popular support had deserted him, he grew ever more bitter.

sentences.zh: 裕素不學，而毅頗涉文雅，故朝土有清望者多歸之，與尚書僕射謝混、丹陽尹郗僧施，深相憑結。

translations.literal: Yu by nature did not study, whereas Yi was fairly versed in refined letters; therefore many court officials of clear reputation turned to him; with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Hun and Danyang Intendant Chi Shishi he formed deep mutual reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had little learning, whereas Yi was well versed in letters; many respected court officials therefore gravitated to him, and he formed a close alliance with Vice Director Xie Hun and Danyang Intendant Chi Shishi.

sentences.zh: 僧施，超之從子也。

translations.literal: Shishi was a nephew of Chi Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Shishi was a nephew of Chi Chao.

sentences.zh: 毅既據上流，陰有圖裕之志，求兼督交、廣二州，裕許之。

translations.literal: Yi, having seized the upper reaches, secretly harbored designs on Yu; he requested concurrent supervision of Jiao and Guang provinces, and Yu granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yi held the upper Yangzi, he secretly plotted against Yu; he requested concurrent supervision of Jiao and Guang provinces, and Yu granted it.

sentences.zh: 毅又奏以郗僧施為南蠻校尉後軍司馬，毛修之為南郡太守，裕亦許之，以劉穆之代僧施為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Yi also memorialized to make Chi Shishi Rear Army Major under the Southern Barbarian Commandant and Mao Xiuzhi Administrator of Nan Commandery; Yu also granted this and made Liu Muzhi replace Shishi as Danyang Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yi also memorialized to appoint Chi Shishi Rear Army Major under the Southern Barbarian Commandant and Mao Xiuzhi Administrator of Nan Commandery; Yu agreed and replaced Shishi with Liu Muzhi as Danyang Intendant.

sentences.zh: 毅表求至京口辭墓，裕往會之於倪塘。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized requesting to go to Jingkou to pay respects at the tombs; Yu went to meet him at Nitang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked permission to go to Jingkou to tend the family tombs; Yu went to meet him at Nitang.

sentences.zh: 寧遠將軍胡籓言於裕曰：「公謂劉衛軍終能為公下乎？」

translations.literal: Pacifying-the-Distance General Hu Fan said to Yu, "Do you think Guard General Liu will ultimately serve under you?"
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-the-Distance General Hu Fan said to Yu, "Do you believe Guard General Liu will ultimately serve under you?"

sentences.zh: 裕默然，久之，曰：「卿謂何如？」

translations.literal: Yu was silent; after a long while he said, "What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu was silent; after a long pause he said, "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 籓曰：「連百萬之眾，攻必取，戰必克，毅固以此服公。

translations.literal: Fan said, "Leading millions of men, attack and you take, fight and you conquer—Yi is indeed convinced by this of you.
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, "Leading armies of millions, you attack and take, fight and conquer—Yi is convinced of that much.

sentences.zh: 至於涉獵傳記，一談一詠，自許以為雄豪；

translations.literal: As for ranging through histories and records, each talk and each verse—he prides himself as a hero;
translations.idiomatic: But in history and poetry, in every conversation and verse, he styles himself a hero;

sentences.zh: 以是搢紳白面之士輻湊歸之。

translations.literal: for this reason gentry and pale-faced scholars converge upon him in crowds.
translations.idiomatic: and for that reason the gentry and literati flock to him.

sentences.zh: 恐終不為公下，不如因會取之。」

translations.literal: I fear he will never serve under you in the end—better to seize him while you have the chance."
translations.idiomatic: I fear he will never truly serve under you—you should seize him while you have the chance."

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「吾與毅俱有克復之功，其過未彰，不可自相圖也。」

translations.literal: Yu said, "Yi and I both have the merit of recovery; his faults are not yet manifest—it is not fitting to plot against each other."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Yi and I both share the merit of restoring the realm; his faults are not yet manifest—we cannot turn on each other."

sentences.zh: 乞伏熾磐攻南涼三河太守吳陰於白土，克之，以乞伏出累代之。

translations.literal: Qifu Chibpan attacked Southern Liang Sanhe Administrator Wu Yin at Baitu, took it, and made Qifu Chulei replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chibpan attacked Wu Yin, Administrator of Sanhe in Southern Liang, at Baitu, took the place, and appointed Qifu Chulei in his stead.

sentences.zh: 六月，乞伏公府弒河南王乾歸，並殺其諸子十餘人，走保大夏。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Qifu Gongfu assassinated Prince of Henan Qifu Gangui and also killed more than ten of his sons, then fled to hold Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Qifu Gongfu assassinated Qifu Gangui, Prince of Henan, and killed more than ten of his sons, then fled to Daxia.

sentences.zh: 平冒公熾磐遣其弟廣武將軍智達、揚武將軍木弈干帥騎三千討之；

translations.literal: Pingchang Duke Chibpan sent his younger brother General Who Displays Martiality Zhida and General Who Displays Martial Prowess Muyigan at the head of three thousand cavalry to campaign against him;
translations.idiomatic: Pingchang Duke Chibpan sent his younger brother General Who Displays Martiality Zhida and General Who Displays Martial Prowess Muyigan with three thousand cavalry against him;

sentences.zh: 以其弟曇達為鎮京將軍，鎮譚郊，驍騎將軍婁機鎮苑川。

translations.literal: he made his younger brother Tanda General Who Guards the Capital to garrison Tanjiao, and Valiant Cavalry General Lou Ji to garrison Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed his younger brother Tanda General Who Guards the Capital at Tanjiao and Valiant Cavalry General Lou Ji at Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 熾磐帥文武及民二萬餘戶遷於枹罕。

translations.literal: Chibpan led civil and military officials and more than twenty thousand households to relocate to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Chibpan relocated his officials and more than twenty thousand households to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 秦人多勸秦王興乘亂取熾磐，興曰：「伐人喪，非禮也。」

translations.literal: Many in Qin urged King Yao Xing to take advantage of the disorder to seize Chibpan; Xing said, "Attacking a man in mourning is not according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Many in Qin urged King Yao Xing to seize Chibpan while he was in disorder; Xing said, "To attack a man in mourning is not proper."

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃欲攻熾磐，軍師中郎將王買德諫曰：「熾磐，吾之與國，今遭喪亂，吾不能恤，又恃眾力而伐之，匹夫且猶恥為，況萬乘乎！」

translations.literal: Xia King Heluobobo wished to attack Chibpan; Army Adviser Commandant Wang Maide remonstrated, saying, "Chibpan is our allied state; now he suffers bereavement and disorder—we cannot succor him, yet if we rely on superior force to attack him, even a common man would be ashamed to do so—how much more a ruler of ten thousand chariots!"
translations.idiomatic: Xia King Heluobobo wished to attack Chibpan; Army Adviser Commandant Wang Maide remonstrated, saying, "Chibpan is our ally; now he suffers bereavement and chaos—we cannot aid him, yet if we rely on superior numbers to attack him, even a common man would be ashamed—how much more a Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 勃勃乃止。

translations.literal: Bobobo thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Heluobobo thereupon desisted.

sentences.zh: 閏月，庚子，南郡烈武公劉道規卒。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on gengzi, Nan Commandery Duke Lie Wu Liu Daogui died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the gengzi day, Liu Daogui, Duke Lie Wu of Nan Commandery, died.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己巳朔，魏主嗣東巡，置四廂大將、十二小將；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day jisi, Wei ruler Si made an eastern tour and established four great generals of the wings and twelve lesser generals;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the first day jisi, Emperor Si of Wei toured east and established four great wing generals and twelve lesser generals;

sentences.zh: 以山陽侯斤、元城侯屈行左、右丞相。

translations.literal: he made Shanyang Marquis Jin and Yuancheng Marquis Qu acting left and right chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: he made Shanyang Marquis Jin and Yuancheng Marquis Qu acting left and right chancellors.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，嗣至濡源，巡西北諸部落。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Si reached Ruyuan and inspected the various tribes of the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day, Si reached Ruyuan and inspected the tribes of the northwest.

sentences.zh: 乞伏智達等擊破乞伏公府於大夏，公府奔疊蘭城，就其弟阿柴。

translations.literal: Qifu Zhida and others defeated Qifu Gongfu at Daxia; Gongfu fled to Dielan City and joined his younger brother Achai.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Zhida and others defeated Qifu Gongfu at Daxia; Gongfu fled to Dielan City to join his younger brother Achai.

sentences.zh: 智達等攻拔之，斬阿柴父子五人。

translations.literal: Zhida and others attacked and took it, beheading Achai and five of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhida and others stormed the city and beheaded Achai and five of his sons.

sentences.zh: 公府奔□□良南山，追獲之，並其四子，轘之於譚郊。

translations.literal: Gongfu fled to the southern mountains of [lacuna]liang; they pursued and captured him, together with his four sons, and dismembered them at Tanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu fled to the southern mountains of [lacuna]liang; they pursued and captured him with his four sons and dismembered them at Tanjiao.

sentences.zh: 八月，乞伏熾磐自稱大將軍、河南王，大赦，改元永康；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Qifu Chibpan styled himself Grand General and Prince of Henan, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongkang;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Qifu Chibpan styled himself Grand General and Prince of Henan, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Yongkang;

sentences.zh: 葬乾歸於枹罕，謚曰武元王，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: he buried Gangui at Fuhan, with posthumous title King Wu Yuan and temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: he buried Gangui at Fuhan with the posthumous title King Wu Yuan and temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang died.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏主嗣還平城。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Wei ruler Si returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, Emperor Si of Wei returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，河南王熾磐以尚書令武始翟勍為相國，侍中、太子詹事趙景為御史大夫；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Prince of Henan Chibpan made Director of the Masters of Writing Zhai Qin of Wushi Chancellor of State, and Attendant-in-Ordinary and Steward of the Heir Apparent Zhao Jing Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Chibpan, Prince of Henan, appointed Director of the Masters of Writing Zhai Qin of Wushi Chancellor of State and Attendant-in-Ordinary and Steward of the Heir Apparent Zhao Jing Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 罷尚書令、僕、尚書六卿、侍中等官。

translations.literal: he abolished the posts of Director of the Masters of Writing, Vice Directors, the six ministers of the Masters of Writing, Attendants-in-Ordinary, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: and abolished the posts of Director and Vice Directors of the Masters of Writing, the six ministers, Attendants-in-Ordinary, and the like.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，葬僖皇后於休平陵。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Reverent Empress was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day, the Reverent Empress was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 劉毅至江陵，多變易守宰，輒割豫州文武、江州兵力萬餘人以自隨。

translations.literal: Liu Yi reached Jiangling, changed many prefects and magistrates, and repeatedly detached more than ten thousand civil and military officials and troops of Yuzhou and Jiangzhou to accompany himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi reached Jiangling, he replaced many prefects and magistrates and took more than ten thousand officials and troops from Yuzhou and Jiangzhou for his own retinue.

sentences.zh: 會毅疾篤，郗僧施等恐毅死，其黨危，乃勸毅請從弟兗州刺史籓以自副，太尉裕偽許之。

translations.literal: As it happened Yi was gravely ill; Chi Shishi and others feared that if Yi died their faction would be endangered, and therefore urged Yi to request his younger cousin by the father's line, Inspector of Yanzhou Fan, as his deputy; Grand Commandant Yu feigned consent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi fell gravely ill, Chi Shishi and others feared that his faction would be endangered if he died and urged him to request his cousin Fan, Inspector of Yanzhou, as deputy; Grand Commandant Yu pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 籓自廣陵入朝，己卯，裕以詔書罪狀毅，雲與籓及謝混共謀不軌，收籓及混賜死。

translations.literal: Fan entered court from Guangling; on jimao, Yu used an imperial edict to enumerate Yi's crimes, stating that he, together with Fan and Xie Hun, had plotted sedition; Fan and Hun were seized and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Fan came to court from Guangling; on the jimao day, Yu issued an edict listing Yi's crimes, declaring that he, Fan, and Xie Hun had plotted rebellion; Fan and Hun were seized and put to death.

sentences.zh: 初，混與劉毅款暱，混從兄澹常以為憂，漸與之疏，謂弟璞及從子瞻曰：「益壽此性，終當破家。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Hun and Liu Yi were intimate in friendship; Hun's elder cousin by the father's line Dan often took this as a worry, gradually grew distant from him, and said to his younger brother Pu and his nephew by the father's line Zhan, "Yishou's nature will in the end destroy the family."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hun and Liu Yi had been close friends; Hun's cousin Dan had often worried about this and gradually grew distant, saying to his brother Pu and his nephew Zhan, "Yishou's character will destroy the family in the end."

sentences.zh: 澹，安之孫也。

translations.literal: Dan was the grandson of Xie An.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was a grandson of Xie An.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔大赦，以前會稽內史司馬休之為都督荊、雍、梁、秦、寧、益六州諸軍事、荊州刺史；

translations.literal: On gengchen, an edict proclaimed a general amnesty; former Kuaiji Interior Minister Sima Xiuzhi was made Area Commander for military affairs in Jing, Yong, Liang, Qin, Ning, and Yi provinces and Inspector of Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day, a general amnesty was proclaimed; former Interior Minister of Kuaiji Sima Xiuzhi was appointed Area Commander over military affairs in Jing, Yong, Liang, Qin, Ning, and Yi provinces and Inspector of Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 北徐州刺史劉道憐為兗、青二州刺史，鎮京口。

translations.literal: Northern Xuzhou Inspector Liu Daolian was made Inspector of Yan and Qing provinces and garrisoned Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daolian, Inspector of Northern Xuzhou, was appointed Inspector of Yan and Qing provinces and stationed at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 使豫州刺史諸葛長民監太尉留府事。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yuzhou Zhuge Changmin was made to oversee the affairs of the Grand Commandant's office left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yuzhou Zhuge Changmin was left to oversee the Grand Commandant's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 裕疑長民難獨任，乃加劉穆之建武將軍，置佐吏，配給資力以防之。

translations.literal: Yu suspected Changmin could not be entrusted alone, and therefore added Liu Muzhi as General Who Establishes Martiality, set up assistant officials, and assigned resources and strength to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu doubted that Changmin could be trusted alone, and therefore appointed Liu Muzhi General Who Establishes Martiality with staff and resources to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 壬午，裕帥諸軍發建康，參軍王鎮惡請給百舸為前驅。

translations.literal: On renwu, Yu led the various armies forth from Jiankang; Army Aide Wang Zhen'e requested a hundred boats as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day, Yu led his armies out of Jiankang; Army Aide Wang Zhen'e asked for a hundred boats as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 丙申，至姑孰，以鎮惡為振武將軍，與龍驤將軍蒯恩將百舸前發。

translations.literal: On bingshen, he reached Gudu, made Zhen'e General Who Quells Martiality, and with Dragon Cavalry General Kuai En led a hundred boats forward.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day, he reached Gudu, appointed Zhen'e General Who Quells Martiality, and sent him forward with Dragon Cavalry General Kuai En at the head of a hundred boats.

sentences.zh: 裕戒之曰：「若賊可擊，擊之；

translations.literal: Yu warned him, saying, "If the bandits can be struck, strike them;
translations.idiomatic: Yu instructed him, "If the enemy can be attacked, attack;

sentences.zh: 不可者，燒其船艦，留屯水際以待我。」

translations.literal: if not, burn their ships and remain encamped at the water's edge to await me."
translations.idiomatic: if not, burn their ships and hold the shore until I arrive."

sentences.zh: 於是鎮惡晝夜兼行，揚聲言劉兗州上。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhen'e marched day and night without rest, proclaiming loudly that Inspector Liu of Yanzhou was coming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e then marched day and night, proclaiming that Inspector Liu of Yanzhou was coming.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己未，鎮惡至豫章口，去江陵城二十里，捨船步上。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiwei, Zhen'e reached Yuzhang Ford, twenty li from Jiangling city; he abandoned the boats and went ashore on foot.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiwei day, Zhen'e reached Yuzhang Ford, twenty li from Jiangling; he left his boats and went ashore.

sentences.zh: 蒯恩軍居前，鎮惡次之。

translations.literal: Kuai En's army was in the van, Zhen'e next.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai En's force led the way, with Zhen'e behind.

sentences.zh: 舸留一二人，對舸岸上立六七旗，旗下置鼓，語所留人：「計我將至城，便鼓嚴，令若後有大軍狀。」

translations.literal: On each boat he left one or two men; on the bank opposite the boats he set up six or seven flags, with drums beneath the flags; he told those left behind, "When you estimate I am about to reach the city, beat the drums in alarm so that it seems a great army follows behind."
translations.idiomatic: On each boat he left one or two men; on the opposite bank he set up six or seven flags with drums beneath them, telling those left behind, "When you judge that I am nearing the city, beat the drums so it seems a great army follows."

sentences.zh: 又分遣人燒江津船艦。

translations.literal: He also sent men separately to burn the ships at Jiang Ford.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent men to burn the ships at Jiang Ford.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡徑前襲城，語前軍士：「有問者，但雲劉兗州至。」

translations.literal: Zhen'e went straight forward to raid the city, telling the vanguard soldiers, "If anyone asks, say only that Inspector Liu of Yanzhou has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e pressed straight on toward the city, telling the vanguard, "If anyone asks, say only that Inspector Liu of Yanzhou has arrived."

sentences.zh: 津戍及民間皆晏然不疑。

translations.literal: The ford garrison and the common people were all tranquil and unsuspecting.
translations.idiomatic: The ford garrison and the people were all calm and unsuspecting.

sentences.zh: 未至城五、六里，逢毅要將朱顯之欲出江津，問：「劉兗州何在？」

translations.literal: When still five or six li from the city, they met Yi's key general Zhu Xianzhi, who wished to go out to Jiang Ford; he asked, "Where is Inspector Liu of Yanzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: When still five or six li from the city, they met Yi's key general Zhu Xianzhi, who was heading for Jiang Ford; he asked, "Where is Inspector Liu of Yanzhou?"

sentences.zh: 軍士曰：「在後。」

translations.literal: The soldiers said, "In the rear."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers said, "In the rear."

sentences.zh: 顯之至軍後，不見籓，而見軍人擔彭排戰具，望江津船艦已被燒，鼓嚴之聲甚盛，知非籓上，便躍馬馳去告毅，行令閉諸城門。

translations.literal: Xianzhi reached the rear of the army but did not see Fan; instead he saw soldiers carrying rattan shields and battle gear; looking toward Jiang Ford he saw the ships already burned and the alarm drums very loud; knowing it was not Fan's arrival, he leapt on his horse and galloped off to inform Yi, ordering all city gates closed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi rode to the rear but saw not Fan but soldiers carrying shields and weapons; he saw the ships at Jiang Ford burning and heard loud drums; knowing it was not Fan, he galloped off to warn Yi and ordered the city gates shut.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡亦馳進，門未及下關，軍人因得入城。

translations.literal: Zhen'e also galloped forward; before the gates could be lowered and barred, the soldiers were able to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e galloped forward too; before the gates could be barred, his men poured into the city.

sentences.zh: 衛軍長史謝純入參承毅，出聞兵至，左右欲引車歸。

translations.literal: Guard Army Chief Clerk Xie Chun entered to attend upon Yi; coming out he heard troops had arrived; those at his sides wished to turn the carriage back.
translations.idiomatic: Guard Army Chief Clerk Xie Chun had gone in to see Yi; coming out he heard troops had arrived, and his attendants wished to turn the carriage back.

sentences.zh: 純叱之曰：「我，人吏也，光將安之！」

translations.literal: Chun rebuked them, saying, "I am a man in office—where would you have me flee!"
translations.idiomatic: Chun rebuked them, saying, "I am a serving official—where would you have me flee!"

sentences.zh: 馳還入府。

translations.literal: He galloped back into the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped back into headquarters.

sentences.zh: 純，安兄據之孫也。

translations.literal: Chun was the grandson of Xie An's elder brother Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was a grandson of Xie An's elder brother Ju.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡與城內兵鬥，且攻其金城。

translations.literal: Zhen'e fought with the troops inside the city and also attacked the Golden City.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e fought the troops in the city and attacked the Golden City.

sentences.zh: 自食時至中晡，城內人敗散。

translations.literal: From mealtime until mid-afternoon the people within the city were defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: From mealtime until mid-afternoon the defenders were defeated and scattered.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡穴其金城而入，遣人以詔及赦文並裕手書示毅，毅皆燒不視，與司馬毛修之等督士卒力戰。

translations.literal: Zhen'e tunneled into the Golden City and entered; he sent men to show Yi the edict, amnesty document, and Yu's own letter; Yi burned them all without looking and, with Major Mao Xiuzhi and others, directed the soldiers to fight with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e breached the Golden City and sent men to show Yi the edict, amnesty, and Yu's personal letter; Yi burned them unread and, with Major Mao Xiuzhi and others, rallied his men to fight on.

sentences.zh: 城內人猶未信裕自來，軍士從毅自東來者，與台軍多中表親戚，且鬥且語，知裕自來，人情離駭。

translations.literal: Those in the city still did not believe Yu had come in person; soldiers who had followed Yi from the east and the capital troops were mostly relatives by marriage; as they fought they also talked, and when they learned Yu had come in person, hearts were divided in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison still did not believe Yu had come in person; many of Yi's eastern troops and the capital forces were related by marriage; as they fought they talked, and when they learned Yu had come himself, morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 逮夜，聽事前兵皆散，斬毅勇將趙蔡，毅左右兵猶閉東西閤拒戰。

translations.literal: By nightfall the troops before the audience hall had all scattered; Yi's brave general Zhao Cai was beheaded; Yi's personal guards still shut the eastern and western wings and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: By nightfall the troops before the audience hall had scattered; Yi's brave general Zhao Cai was killed; only Yi's personal guards still held the eastern and western wings and fought on.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡慮暗中自相傷犯，乃引軍出圍金城，開其南面。

translations.literal: Zhen'e feared that in the darkness they would injure one another by mistake; he therefore led his army out to surround the Golden City and opened its south side.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing friendly fire in the dark, Zhen'e withdrew his men to encircle the Golden City and opened its southern gate.

sentences.zh: 毅慮南有伏兵，夜半，帥左右三百許人開北門突出。

translations.literal: Yi feared ambush to the south; at midnight he led about three hundred of his close followers to open the north gate and break out.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting an ambush to the south, Yi at midnight led some three hundred trusted men out through the north gate.

sentences.zh: 毛修之謂謝純曰：「君但隨僕去。」

translations.literal: Mao Xiuzhi said to Xie Chun, "My lord, simply follow me and go."
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi told Xie Chun, "Just come with me."

sentences.zh: 純不從，為人所殺。

translations.literal: Chun did not obey and was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: Chun refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 毅夜投牛牧佛寺。

translations.literal: By night Yi fled to Niuchu Buddhist Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yi sought refuge at Niuchu Temple.

sentences.zh: 初，桓蔚之敗也，走投牛牧寺僧昌，昌保藏之，毅殺昌。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan Wei was defeated, he fled in distress to Niuchu Temple monk Chang; Chang concealed him, and Yi killed Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Huan Wei's defeat, he had fled to Niuchu Temple, where the monk Chang hid him; Yi had Chang executed.

sentences.zh: 至是，寺僧拒之曰：「昔亡師容桓蔚，為劉衛軍所殺，今實不敢容異人。」

translations.literal: At this time the temple monks rejected him, saying, "In the past our deceased master sheltered Huan Wei and was killed by Guard Army Liu; now we truly dare not shelter an outsider."
translations.idiomatic: Now the monks turned him away, saying, "Our late master once sheltered Huan Wei and was killed by Liu Yi; we dare not take in a stranger now."

sentences.zh: 毅歎曰：「為法自弊，一至於此！」

translations.literal: Yi sighed and said, "Applying the law brought ruin on myself—matters have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi sighed, "I brought this on myself by enforcing the law—how far it has come!"

sentences.zh: 遂縊而死。

translations.literal: He then hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 明日，居人以告，乃斬首於市，並子侄皆伏誅。

translations.literal: The next day residents reported it; his head was then cut off and displayed in the market, and his sons and nephews were all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The next day townspeople reported his body; his head was cut off and displayed in the market, and his sons and nephews were all executed.

sentences.zh: 毅兄模奔襄陽，魯宗之斬送之。

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother Mo fled to Xiangyang; Lu Zongzhi beheaded him and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's elder brother Mo fled to Xiangyang; Lu Zongzhi killed him and sent his head in.

sentences.zh: 初，毅季父鎮之閒居京口，不應辟召，常謂毅及籓曰：「汝輩才器，足以得志，但恐不久耳。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yi's younger uncle Zhenzhi lived in retirement at Jingkou and did not respond to summons; he often said to Yi and Fan, "Your talents and capacities are enough to achieve your ambitions, but I fear it will not be for long.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's uncle Zhenzhi had lived quietly at Jingkou, refusing office; he often told Yi and Fan, "Your talent is enough to fulfill your ambitions—but I doubt it will last long.

sentences.zh: 我不就爾求財位，亦不同爾受罪累。」

translations.literal: I do not seek from you wealth and rank, nor do I share with you the burden of punishment."
translations.idiomatic: I won't ask you for riches or office, and I won't share your punishment when it comes."

sentences.zh: 每見毅、籓導從到門。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw Yi and Fan arrive at the gate with their escorts and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yi and Fan arrived at his gate with their entourage—

sentences.zh: 輒詬之，毅甚敬畏，未至宅數百步，悉屏儀衛，與白衣數人俱進。

translations.literal: he would revile them; Yi was very awed and reverent, and several hundred paces before reaching the house he would dismiss all guards of honor and enter with only a few men in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: he would scold them. Yi held him in deep awe; hundreds of paces from the house he dismissed his full escort and entered with only a few attendants in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 及毅死，太尉裕奏征鎮之為散騎常侍、光祿大夫，固辭不至。

translations.literal: When Yi died, Grand Commandant Yu memorialized to summon Zhenzhi as Palace Attendant and Grandee of Splendid Happiness; he firmly declined and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yi's death, Liu Yu recommended Zhenzhi for court office; Zhenzhi steadfastly refused to come.

sentences.zh: 仇池公楊盛叛秦，侵擾祁山。

translations.literal: Duke of Chouchi Yang Sheng rebelled against Qin and harassed Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, rebelled against Qin and raided Qishan.

sentences.zh: 秦王興遣建威將軍趙琨為前鋒，立節將軍姚伯壽繼之，前將軍姚恢出鷲峽，秦州刺史姚暠出羊頭峽，右衛將軍胡翼度出汧城，以討盛。

translations.literal: King Xing of Qin sent General Who Establishes Might Zhao Kun as vanguard, General Who Upholds Integrity Yao Boshou to follow, Former General Yao Hui out through Jiu Pass, Qinzhou Inspector Yao Hao out through Yangtou Pass, and Right Guard General Hu Yidu out through Qian city, to attack Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: King Yao Xing of Qin sent Zhao Kun as vanguard with Yao Boshou in support, Yao Hui through Jiu Pass, Yao Hao through Yangtou Pass, and Hu Yidu through Qian, to suppress Yang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 興自雍赴之，與諸將會於隴口。

translations.literal: Xing himself went from Yong to join them and met the generals at Longkou.
translations.idiomatic: Xing marched from Yong and joined his generals at Longkou.

sentences.zh: 天水太守王松匆言於嵩曰：「先帝神略無方，徐洛生以英武佐命，再入仇池，無功而還；

translations.literal: Tianshui Administrator Wang Song spoke hastily to Song, saying, "The late emperor's divine strategy was without limit; Xu Luosheng, with heroic martial prowess assisting fate, entered Chouchi twice and returned without success;
translations.idiomatic: Tianshui Administrator Wang Song urgently told Yao Song, "The late emperor's strategy was unmatched; even Xu Luosheng, heroic and entrusted with the throne's support, twice invaded Chouchi and came back empty-handed—

sentences.zh: 非楊氏智勇難全也，直地勢險固耳。

translations.literal: it was not that the Yang clan's wisdom and courage were hard to overcome—only that the terrain was perilous and firm.
translations.idiomatic: not because the Yangs were invincible, but because the ground was too treacherous.

sentences.zh: 今以趙琨之眾，使君之威，准之先朝，實未見成功。

translations.literal: Now with Zhao Kun's force and Your Lordship's authority, measured against the former court, success is truly not in sight.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhao Kun's army and your prestige, I see no better prospect of success than in the past.

sentences.zh: 使君具悉形便，何不表聞！」

translations.literal: Your Lordship fully knows the terrain's advantages—why not memorialize and report it!"
translations.idiomatic: You know the terrain as well as anyone—why not report this to the throne!"

sentences.zh: 嵩不從。

translations.literal: Song did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Song paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 盛帥眾與琨相持，伯壽畏懦不進，琨眾寡不敵，為盛所敗。

translations.literal: Sheng led his forces to face Kun in a standoff; Boshou was timid and cowardly and did not advance; Kun's numbers were few and could not match; he was defeated by Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng confronted Zhao Kun, but Yao Boshou hung back in fear; outnumbered, Kun was defeated.

sentences.zh: 興斬伯壽而還。

translations.literal: Xing beheaded Boshou and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xing executed Boshou and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 興以楊佛嵩為雍州刺史，帥嶺北見兵以擊夏。

translations.literal: Xing made Yang Fosu Inspector of Yongzhou and led the available troops north of the ridges to attack Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Xing appointed Yang Fosu Inspector of Yongzhou and sent him with the troops north of the ridges against Xia.

sentences.zh: 行數日，興謂群臣曰：「佛嵩每見敵，勇不自制，吾常節其兵不過五千人。

translations.literal: After several days on the march, Xing said to his ministers, "Fosu whenever he sees the enemy cannot restrain his bravery; I always limit his troops to no more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After several days' march, Xing told his ministers, "Fosu loses all restraint when he sees the enemy; I always cap his command at five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 今所將既多，遇敵必敗，行已遠，追之無及，將若之何？」

translations.literal: Now the force he leads is already large; meeting the enemy he will surely be defeated; he has already gone far, and it is too late to pursue and recall him—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Now he leads too many men—he is bound to lose when he meets the enemy, and he is too far away to recall. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 佛嵩與夏王勃勃戰，果敗，為勃勃所執，絕亢而死。

translations.literal: Fosu fought with Xia King Heluobobo and was indeed defeated; he was seized by Heluobobo and died with his neck broken.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fosu fought Heluobobo and lost; captured, he was executed by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 秦立昭儀齊氏為後。

translations.literal: Qin installed Consort Qi as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Qin elevated Lady Qi from palace lady to empress.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜遷於姑臧。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun moved his seat to Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun relocated his capital to Guzang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己卯，太尉裕至江陵，殺郗僧施。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jimao, Grand Commandant Yu reached Jiangling and killed Xi Shenshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the jimao day, Liu Yu reached Jiangling and executed Xi Shenshi.

sentences.zh: 初，毛修之雖為劉毅僚佐。

translations.literal: Earlier, though Mao Xiuzhi had been Liu Yi's subordinate officer.
translations.idiomatic: Though Mao Xiuzhi had served as Liu Yi's aide,

sentences.zh: 素自結於裕，故裕特宥之。

translations.literal: he had long attached himself to Yu; therefore Yu specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: he had long cultivated ties with Liu Yu, who therefore spared him.

sentences.zh: 賜王鎮惡爵漢壽子。

translations.literal: He granted Wang Zhen'e the noble rank of Marquis of Hanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu ennobled Wang Zhen'e as Marquis of Hanshou.

sentences.zh: 裕問毅府咨議參軍申永曰：「今日何施而可？」

translations.literal: Yu asked Yi's staff Adviser Shen Yong, "What measures should be taken today?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu asked Shen Yong, Yi's former staff adviser, "What should be done now?"

sentences.zh: 永曰：「除其宿畔，倍其惠澤，貫敘門次，顯擢才能，如此而已。」

translations.literal: Yong said, "Remove old grudges, double beneficent grace, arrange ranks by seniority, and clearly promote ability—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yong replied, "Pardon old enmities, redouble your kindness, restore order by rank, and promote the able—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 裕納之，下書寬租省調，節役原刑，禮辟名士，荊人悅之。

translations.literal: Yu accepted this; he issued orders to lighten rents and reduce levies, limit corvée and remit punishments, and honor and recruit notable men; the people of Jing were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu took his advice: he reduced taxes and levies, eased labor and punishments, and honored worthy men; the people of Jingzhou rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 諸葛長民驕縱貪侈，所為多不法，為百姓患，常懼太尉裕按之。

translations.literal: Zhuge Changmin was arrogant, unrestrained, and greedy and extravagant; his actions were often unlawful and an affliction to the common people; he constantly feared that Grand Commandant Yu would investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin was arrogant, greedy, and often lawless—a plague on the people—and he lived in fear that Liu Yu would move against him.

sentences.zh: 及劉毅被誅，長民謂所親曰：「『昔年醢彭越，今年殺韓信。』

translations.literal: When Liu Yi was executed, Changmin said to those close to him, "‘Last year Peng Yue was made into mincemeat; this year Han Xin was killed.’
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi was executed, Changmin told his intimates, "‘Last year they minced Peng Yue; this year they killed Han Xin.’

sentences.zh: 禍其至矣！」

translations.literal: Disaster is about to arrive!"
translations.idiomatic: My turn is coming!"

sentences.zh: 乃屏人問劉穆之曰：「悠悠之言，皆雲太尉與我不平，何以至此？」

translations.literal: He then dismissed others and asked Liu Muzhi, "Idle talk everywhere says the Grand Commandant and I are at odds—how did it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: In private he asked Liu Muzhi, "Everyone says Liu Yu has turned against me—how did it come to this?"

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「公溯流遠征，以老母稚子委節下。

translations.literal: Muzhi said, "The Duke went upriver on a distant campaign and entrusted his old mother and young children to Your Excellency's care.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi said, "He marched far upriver and left his mother and children in your hands.

sentences.zh: 若一豪不盡，豈容如此邪！」

translations.literal: If not a single able man had been left behind, how could he have permitted such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: If he had kept even one strong man behind, would he have dared act as he did?"

sentences.zh: 長民意乃小安。

translations.literal: Changmin's mind was then somewhat settled.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin was somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 長民弟輔國大將軍黎民說長民曰：「劉氏之亡，亦諸葛氏之懼也，宜因裕未還而圖之。」

translations.literal: Changmin's younger brother, General Who Assists the State Li Min, urged Changmin, saying, "The Liu clan's destruction is also the Zhuge clan's fear; you should take advantage of Yu's not yet having returned to plot against him."
translations.idiomatic: Changmin's brother Li Min urged him, "If the Lius fall, the Zhuges are next—you should strike while Liu Yu is still away."

sentences.zh: 長民猶豫未發，既而歎曰：「貧賤常思富貴，富貴必履危機。

translations.literal: Changmin hesitated and did not act; then he sighed and said, "In poverty one always longs for wealth and rank; in wealth and rank one must tread on peril's brink.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin hesitated. At last he sighed, "The poor dream of wealth; the wealthy walk among dangers.

sentences.zh: 今日欲為丹徒布衣。

translations.literal: Today I wish to become a common cloth-wearer of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Today I would gladly be a commoner in Dantu again.

sentences.zh: 豈可得邪！」

translations.literal: How could that be obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: But that is no longer possible!"

sentences.zh: 因遺冀州刺史劉敬宣書曰：「盤龍狠戾專恣，自取夷滅。

translations.literal: He therefore sent a letter to Jizhou Inspector Liu Jingxuan, saying, "Pan Long was brutal, arrogant, and willful and brought extinction on himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Liu Jingxuan, "Pan Long's cruelty and arrogance destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 異端將盡，世路方夷，富貴之事，相與共之。」

translations.literal: The heterodox faction is nearly exhausted; the world's path is now level; matters of wealth and rank—let us share them together."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are nearly gone and the path ahead is clear—let us share what fortune brings."

sentences.zh: 敬宣報曰：「下官自義熙以來，忝三州、七郡，常懼福過災生，思避盈居損。

translations.literal: Jingxuan replied, "Your humble servant since Yixi has undeservedly held three provinces and seven commanderies; I have constantly feared that blessings excessive would bring disaster arising, and thought to avoid fullness and abide in modesty.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan replied, "Since Yixi I have undeservedly held three provinces and seven commanderies; I have always feared that too much good fortune invites disaster, and sought humility over excess.

sentences.zh: 富貴之旨，非所敢當。」

translations.literal: Your message on wealth and rank is not what I dare accept."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not accept your offer of shared fortune."

sentences.zh: 且使以書呈裕，裕曰：「阿壽故為不負我也。」

translations.literal: He also had the letter presented to Yu; Yu said, "Ashou indeed has not failed me."
translations.idiomatic: He forwarded the letter to Liu Yu, who said, "Ashou has proved true to me after all."

sentences.zh: 劉穆之憂長民為變，屏人問太尉行參軍東海何承天曰：「公今行濟否？」

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi, worried that Changmin would rebel, dismissed others and asked Grand Commandant's traveling aide He Chengtian of Donghai, "Will the Duke's journey succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Fearing rebellion from Zhuge Changmin, Liu Muzhi privately asked He Chengtian, "Will the Duke's return succeed?"

sentences.zh: 承天曰：「荊州不憂不時判，別有一慮耳。

translations.literal: Chengtian said, "Jingzhou need not worry—it will not fail to submit in due course; there is only one other concern.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian said, "Jingzhou is no worry—it will come over without delay. Only one thing troubles me.

sentences.zh: 公昔年自左裡還入石頭，甚脫爾；
