translations.literal: When you returned from Zuoli into Stone City in former years, you were very unguarded and casual;
translations.idiomatic: When you returned from Zuoli to Stone City before, you were far too relaxed;

sentences.zh: 今還，宜加重慎。」

translations.literal: now on your return you should redouble caution."
translations.idiomatic: this time you must be far more careful."

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「非君，不聞此言。」

translations.literal: Muzhi said, "But for you, I would not have heard these words."
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi said, "Without you, I would never have heard this."

sentences.zh: 裕在江陵，輔國將軍王誕白裕求先下，裕曰：「諸葛長民似有自疑心，卿言巨宜便去！」

translations.literal: Yu was at Jiangling; General Who Assists the State Wang Dan reported to Yu asking to go down ahead; Yu said, "Zhuge Changmin seems to have self-suspicion in his heart; as you say, you should go at once!"
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling, Wang Dan asked leave to go on ahead. Liu Yu said, "Zhuge Changmin seems suspicious of us—you should go at once, as you suggest!"

sentences.zh: 誕曰：「長民知我蒙公垂眄，今輕身單下，必當以為無虞，乃可以少安其意耳。」

translations.literal: Dan said, "Changmin knows I enjoy the Duke's gracious favor; if I now go down lightly alone, he will surely think there is nothing to worry about—and so his mind can be somewhat calmed."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan said, "Changmin knows you favor me. If I go on alone, he will think there is no danger—and that may ease his mind."

sentences.zh: 裕笑曰：「卿勇過賁、育矣。」

translations.literal: Yu smiled and said, "Your courage surpasses Ben and Yu!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu laughed, "Your courage outdoes Ben and Yu!"

sentences.zh: 乃聽先還。

translations.literal: He then permitted him to return first.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu allowed him to go ahead.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜即河西王位，大赦，改元玄始，置官僚如涼王光為三河王故事。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun took the title King of Hexi, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Xuanshi, and established officials and bureaucracy following the precedent when King Guang of Liang became King of Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun declared himself King of Hexi, issued an amnesty, adopted the era name Xuanshi, and organized a court on the model Lv Guang had used as King of Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕謀伐蜀，擇元帥而難其人。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yu planned to attack Shu, chose a commander-in-chief but found the right man hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu planned an expedition against Shu but struggled to find the right commander.

sentences.zh: 以西陽太守朱齡石既有武干，又練吏職，欲用之。

translations.literal: Because Xiyang Administrator Zhu Lingqi had both martial capacity and was skilled in administrative office, he wished to use him.
translations.idiomatic: He favored Xiyang Administrator Zhu Lingqi, who combined military talent with administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 眾皆以為齡石資名尚輕，難當重任，裕不從。

translations.literal: The multitude all thought Lingqi's qualifications and reputation were still light and that he would find it hard to bear heavy responsibility; Yu did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Others thought Zhu Lingqi too junior in rank and reputation for so great a task; Liu Yu disagreed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以齡石為益州刺史，帥寧朔將軍臧熹、河間太守蒯恩、下邳太守劉鐘等伐蜀，分大軍之半二萬人以配之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he made Lingqi Inspector of Yizhou and, leading General Who Calms the North Zang Xi, Hejian Administrator Kuai En, Xiapi Administrator Liu Zhong, and others to attack Shu, assigned him half of the great army—twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he appointed Zhu Lingqi Inspector of Yizhou and sent him against Shu with Zang Xi, Kuai En, Liu Zhong, and twenty thousand men—half the main army.

sentences.zh: 熹，裕之妻弟，位居齡石之右，亦隸焉。

translations.literal: Xi was Yu's wife's younger brother; his rank stood to Lingqi's right and he was also subordinate to the command.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xi, Liu Yu's brother-in-law, outranked Zhu Lingqi but served under his command.

sentences.zh: 裕與齡石密謀進取，曰：「劉敬宣往年出黃虎，無功而退。

translations.literal: Yu secretly planned the advance with Lingqi, saying, "Liu Jingxuan in former years went out through Huanghu and returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu confided his strategy to Zhu Lingqi: "When Liu Jingxuan marched through Huanghu he failed.

sentences.zh: 賊謂我今應從外水往，而料我當出其不意猶從內水來也。

translations.literal: The enemy thinks that today we should go by the outer water route, yet reckons we will still take them by surprise and come by the inner water.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy expects us on the outer route but will still assume we may surprise them via the inner route.

sentences.zh: 如此，必以重兵守涪城以備內道。

translations.literal: If so, they will surely use heavy troops to guard Fucheng to secure the inner route.
translations.idiomatic: They will mass troops at Fucheng to block the inner route.

sentences.zh: 若向黃虎，正墮其計。

translations.literal: If we head toward Huanghu, we will exactly fall into their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Marching on Huanghu would play into their hands.

sentences.zh: 今以大眾自外水取成都，疑兵出內水，此制敵之奇也。」

translations.literal: Now with the main force take Chengdu by the outer water, and with a diversionary force show ourselves on the inner water—this is the marvel of controlling the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Send the main army against Chengdu by the outer water while a feint threatens the inner route—that is how we turn their expectations against them."

sentences.zh: 而慮此聲先馳，賊審虛實。

translations.literal: Yet he feared this plan would run ahead by rumor and the enemy would discern the empty and the real.
translations.idiomatic: But he feared word of this would spread first and let the enemy learn his true intent.

sentences.zh: 別有函書封付齡石，署函邊曰：「至白帝乃開。」

translations.literal: Separately he had a sealed letter made and entrusted to Lingqi; on the edge of the envelope he wrote, "Open only upon reaching Baidi."
translations.idiomatic: He gave Zhu Lingqi a sealed letter marked "Open at Baidi."

sentences.zh: 諸軍雖進，未知處分所由。

translations.literal: Though the armies advanced, they did not know by what orders they were to act.
translations.idiomatic: The armies marched on without knowing their final orders.

sentences.zh: 毛修之固請行，裕恐修之至蜀，必多所誅殺，土人與毛氏有嫌，亦當以死自固，不許。

translations.literal: Mao Xiuzhi firmly requested to go on the campaign; Yu feared that when Xiuzhi reached Shu he would surely put many to death; the native people had grudges against the Mao clan, and they too would fight to the death to hold firm—he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi begged to join the expedition, but Liu Yu feared he would slaughter locals in Shu—the Mao clan had enemies there who would resist to the death—so he refused.

sentences.zh: 分荊州十郡置湘州。

translations.literal: Ten commanderies of Jingzhou were split off to establish Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ten commanderies were carved from Jingzhou to form Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 加太尉裕太傅、揚州牧。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yu was additionally made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was further appointed Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，魏主嗣北巡，至長城而還。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Wei Ruler Si toured north, reached the Great Wall, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day, Emperor Si of Wei toured the north as far as the Great Wall and returned.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝辛義熙九年（

translations.literal: Emperor An, Xin, ninth year of Yixi (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An, ninth year of Yixi (

sentences.zh: 癸丑，公元四一三年）

translations.literal: guichou, the year 413 CE)
translations.idiomatic: guichou, 413 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，庚戌，魏主嗣如高柳川。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on gengxu, Wei Ruler Si went to Gaoliu River.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the gengxu day of the second month, Emperor Si of Wei went to Gaoliu River.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，還宮。

translations.literal: On jiayin, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕自江陵東還，駱驛遣輜重兼行而下，前刻至日，每淹留不進。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yu returned east from Jiangling, dispatching baggage by relay stages in rapid combined travel downriver; for the previously announced day of arrival, he each time delayed and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu headed east from Jiangling, sending his baggage train ahead by rapid stages while he himself lingered, missing each announced date of arrival.

sentences.zh: 諸葛長民與公卿頻日奉候於新亭，輒差其期。

translations.literal: Zhuge Changmin and the ministers for many days attended and waited at Xinting, but he each time missed the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin and the court officials waited day after day at Xinting, only to be stood up again and again.

sentences.zh: 乙丑晦，裕輕舟徑進，潛入東府。

translations.literal: On the last day of yichou, Yu in a light boat went straight forward and secretly entered the Eastern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the last night of yichou, Liu Yu slipped into the Eastern Headquarters by swift boat.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙寅朔旦，長民聞之，驚趨至門。

translations.literal: In the third month, at dawn on the first day bingyin, Changmin heard of it and rushed in alarm to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the first day of the third month, bingyin, Changmin learned of his arrival and rushed to the gate in alarm.

sentences.zh: 裕伏壯土丁晤於幔中，引長民卻人閒語，凡平生所不盡者皆及之，長民甚悅。

translations.literal: Yu hid the stalwart Ding Wu behind a curtain; he drew Changmin aside for private conversation and touched on all that had gone unsaid through their lives; Changmin was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu hid the strongman Ding Wu behind a curtain, drew Changmin aside for a private talk covering everything left unsaid between them—and Changmin was delighted.

sentences.zh: 丁晤自幔後出，於座拉殺之，輿屍付廷尉。

translations.literal: Ding Wu came out from behind the curtain and at the seat seized and killed him; the corpse was loaded on a cart and delivered to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wu emerged from behind the curtain and killed him on the spot; his body was sent to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 收其弟黎民，黎民素驍勇，格鬥而死。

translations.literal: They arrested his younger brother Li Min; Li Min had always been fierce and brave and died fighting hand to hand.
translations.idiomatic: They seized his brother Li Min, a renowned fighter, who died in the struggle.

sentences.zh: 並殺其季弟大司馬參軍幼民、從弟寧朔將軍秀之。

translations.literal: They also killed his youngest brother, Grand Marshal Staff Officer Youmin, and his cousin, General Who Calms the North Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: They also killed his youngest brother Youmin and his cousin Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 庚午，秦王興遣使至魏修好。

translations.literal: On gengwu, King Xing of Qin sent envoys to Wei to restore friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day, King Yao Xing of Qin sent envoys to Wei to renew amity.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕上表曰：「大司馬溫以『民無定本，傷治為深』，《庚戌》土斷以一其業。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yu submitted a memorial, saying, "Grand Marshal Wen, because 'the people have no fixed attachment; harm to governance is deep,' used the Gengxu land resettlement to unify their holdings.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu memorialized the throne: "Grand Marshal Wen held that 'without fixed roots among the people, governance suffers deeply,' and the Gengxu land allotment edict unified households in their places of origin.

sentences.zh: 於是財阜國豐，實由於此。

translations.literal: Thereupon wealth was abundant and the state flourished—in truth this was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: From that came national wealth and strength—and this was the source.

sentences.zh: 自茲迄今，漸用頹馳；

translations.literal: From then until now, use of it has gradually collapsed and slackened;
translations.idiomatic: Since then the practice has steadily decayed;

sentences.zh: 請申前制。」

translations.literal: I request that the former regulation be enforced again."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the earlier land-allotment rules be enforced once more."

sentences.zh: 於是依界土斷，唯徐、兗、青三州居晉陵者，不在斷例；

translations.literal: Thereupon they resettled land according to native borders; only those from Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces residing at Jinling were exempt from the resettlement rule;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon land was allotted according to native borders; only immigrants from Xu, Yan, and Qing who lived at Jinling were exempt from the resettlement provisions;

sentences.zh: 諸流寓郡縣多所並省。

translations.literal: Many of the refugee districts and counties were merged or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Many districts and counties of resettled refugees were abolished or consolidated.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，加裕豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Yu was additionally appointed Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Liu Yu was additionally appointed Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 裕固讓太傅、州牧。

translations.literal: Yu firmly declined the posts of Grand Tutor and Regional Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu firmly declined the posts of Grand Tutor and Regional Governor.

sentences.zh: 林邑范胡達寇九真，杜慧度擊斬之。

translations.literal: Fan Huda of Linyi raided Jiuzhen; Du Huidu attacked and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Huda of Linyi raided Jiuzhen; Du Huidu attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 河南王熾磐遣鎮東將軍曇達、平東將軍王松壽將兵東擊休官權小郎、呂破胡於白石川，大破之，虜其男女萬餘口，進據白石城。

translations.literal: The Prince of Henan, Qifu Chifen, sent the General Who Pacifies the East Tanda and the General Who Pacifies the East Wang Songsou with troops east to attack the Xiuguan Qian Xiaolang and Lu Pohu at Baishi River; he utterly defeated them, captured more than ten thousand men and women, and advanced to occupy Baishi City.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Henan Qifu Chifen sent Generals Who Pacify the East Tanda and Wang Songsou east against the Xiuguan leaders Qian Xiaolang and Lu Pohu at Baishi River, routed them, took more than ten thousand captives, and seized Baishi City.

sentences.zh: 顯親休官權小成、呂奴迦等二萬餘戶據白坑不服，曇達攻斬之，隴右休官悉降。

translations.literal: More than twenty thousand households of the Xiuguan—Qian Xiaocheng and Lu Nujia of Xianqin and others—held Baikeng and refused submission; Tanda attacked and killed them, and all the Xiuguan of Longyou submitted.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty thousand Xiuguan households under Qian Xiaocheng and Lu Nujia of Xianqin held out at Baikeng; Tanda attacked and killed them, after which all the Xiuguan of Longyou submitted.

sentences.zh: 秦太尉索稜以隴西降熾磐，熾磐以稜為太傅。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Suo Ling of Qin surrendered Longxi to Chifen; Chifen made Ling Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Grand Commandant Suo Ling surrendered Longxi to Chifen, who appointed him Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃大赦，改元鳳翔。

translations.literal: The Xia king Heluobobo proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xia King Heluobobo proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 以叱干阿利領將作大匠，發嶺北夷、夏十萬人築都城於朔方水北、黑水之南。

translations.literal: He appointed Chigan Ali to lead the Director of Works, mobilizing a hundred thousand Yi and Xia people north of the ranges to build a capital on the north bank of the Shuofang River and south of the Black Water.
translations.idiomatic: He made Chigan Ali Director of Works and mobilized a hundred thousand tribal peoples north of the ranges to build a capital on the north bank of the Shuofang River and south of the Black Water.

sentences.zh: 勃勃曰：「朕方統一天下，君臨萬邦，宜名新城曰統萬。」

translations.literal: Heluobobo said, "I am now unifying the realm and ruling over ten thousand states; the new city should be named Tongwan."」
translations.idiomatic: Heluobobo said, "I mean to unify the realm and rule the nations—this new city should be called Tongwan."」

sentences.zh: 阿利性巧而殘忍，蒸土築城，錐入一寸，即殺作者而並築之。

translations.literal: Ali was skillful by nature but cruel; building the wall of steamed earth, if an awl could be driven in one inch, he would kill the builder and incorporate the body into the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Ali was ingenious but brutal: he built walls of steamed earth, and if an awl could penetrate an inch, he killed the workman and built his corpse into the wall.

sentences.zh: 勃勃以為忠，委任之。

translations.literal: Heluobobo considered this loyalty and entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Heluobobo took this for loyalty and gave him full authority.

sentences.zh: 凡造兵器成，呈之，工人必有死者，射甲不入則斬弓人，入則斬甲匠。

translations.literal: Whenever weapons were completed and presented, a worker would invariably die; if an arrow did not pierce the armor, the bow-maker was beheaded; if it did pierce, the armorer was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever finished weapons were presented, some craftsman always died: if an arrow failed to pierce the armor, the bow-maker was beheaded; if it did pierce, the armorer was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 又鑄銅為一大鼓。

translations.literal: He also cast a great bronze drum.
translations.idiomatic: He also cast a great bronze drum.

sentences.zh: 飛廉、翁仲、銅駝、龍虎之屬，飾以黃金，列於宮殿之前。

translations.literal: Images of Feilian, Wengzhong, bronze camels, dragons and tigers, and the like were ornamented with gold and arrayed before the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Statues of Feilian, Wengzhong, bronze camels, dragons, tigers, and the like were gilded and set before the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 凡殺工匠數千，由是器物皆精利。

translations.literal: In all several thousand craftsmen were killed; from this the vessels and implements were all fine and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: He killed several thousand craftsmen in all; because of this, every object produced was exquisitely finished.

sentences.zh: 勃勃自謂其祖從母姓為劉，非禮也。

translations.literal: Heluobobo held that his ancestor's taking his mother's surname Liu was contrary to propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Heluobobo held that his ancestors' adoption of the maternal surname Liu was improper.

sentences.zh: 古從氏族無常，乃改姓赫連氏，言帝王系天為子，其徽赫與天連也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the surname taken from one's clan had no fixed rule; so he changed his surname to Helian, meaning that emperors and kings were attached to Heaven as sons, their grandeur linked with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Since clans in antiquity had no fixed surnames, he changed his own to Helian, declaring that emperors are Heaven's sons and that his glory links him with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其非正統者，皆以鐵伐為氏，言其剛銳如鐵，皆堪伐人也。

translations.literal: Those of non-orthodox lines all took Tiefa as their clan name, meaning they were hard and sharp as iron—all fit to slay men.
translations.idiomatic: Non-royal clans were all given the surname Tiefa, "Iron Slayer," meaning they were hard as iron and born to kill.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙卯，魏主嗣西巡，命鄭兵將奚斤、鴻飛將軍尉古真、都將閭大肥等擊越勤部於跋那山。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, Wei ruler Si made a western tour and ordered the Zheng troops commander Xi Jin, General Who Flies Like a Swan Yu Guzheng, and Chief commander Lu Dafei and others to attack the Yueqin tribe at Bana Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on yimao, Wei Emperor Si toured the west and ordered Zheng contingent commander Xi Jin, General Who Flies Like a Swan Yu Guzheng, Chief commander Lu Dafei, and others to attack the Yueqin at Bana Mountain.

sentences.zh: 大肥，柔然人也。

translations.literal: Dafei was a man of Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Dafei was a Rouran.

sentences.zh: 河南王熾磐遣安北將軍烏地延、冠軍將軍翟紹擊吐谷渾別統句旁於泣勤川，大破之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Henan, Qifu Chifen, sent the General Who Pacifies the North Wudiyan and the General Who Conquers the Champions Zhai Shao to attack the Tuyuhun sub-commander Ju Pang at Qiqin River and utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Henan Qifu Chifen sent Generals Who Pacify the North Wudiyan and Who Conquer Ju Pang, a Tuyuhun sub-commander, at Qiqin River and routed him.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜立子政德為世子，加鎮衛大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hexi, Meng Xun, established his son Zhengde as heir apparent and added the titles General Who Guards and Protects the Realm and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi Prince Meng Xun named his son Zhengde heir apparent and made him General Who Guards the Realm and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 南涼王辱檀伐河西王蒙遜，蒙遜敗之於若厚塢，又敗之於若涼；

translations.literal: The Prince of Southern Liang, Rutan, attacked the Prince of Hexi, Meng Xun; Meng Xun defeated him at Ruohouwu and again at Ruoliang;
translations.idiomatic: Southern Liang Prince Rutan attacked Hexi Prince Meng Xun, who defeated him at Ruohouwu and again at Ruoliang;

sentences.zh: 因進圍樂都，二旬不克。

translations.literal: Then he advanced to besiege Ledu; in twenty days he did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Ledu but failed to take it in twenty days.

sentences.zh: 南涼湟河太守文支以郡降於蒙遜，蒙遜以文支為廣武太守。

translations.literal: Wenzhi, Administrator of Huanghe in Southern Liang, surrendered the commandery to Meng Xun; Meng Xun made Wenzhi Administrator of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhi, governor of Huanghe in Southern Liang, surrendered his commandery to Meng Xun, who appointed him governor of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜復伐南涼，辱檀以太尉俱延為質，乃還。

translations.literal: Meng Xun again attacked Southern Liang; Rutan gave Grand Commandant Juyan as hostage, and Meng Xun then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun attacked Southern Liang again; Rutan handed over Grand Commandant Juyan as a hostage, and Meng Xun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜西如苕台，遣冠軍將軍伏恩將騎一萬襲卑和、烏啼二部，大破之，俘二千餘落而還。

translations.literal: Meng Xun went west to Tiaotai and sent the General Who Conquers Fu En with ten thousand cavalry to raid the Beihe and Wuti tribes; he utterly defeated them, captured more than two thousand households, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun went west to Tiaotai and sent General Who Conquers Fu En with ten thousand horsemen against the Beihe and Wuti tribes, routed them, took more than two thousand clans captive, and returned.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜寢於新台，閹人王懷祖擊蒙遜，傷足，其妻孟氏禽斬之。

translations.literal: Meng Xun was asleep on the New Tower; the eunuch Wang Huaizu struck Meng Xun and wounded his foot; his wife Lady Meng seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: While Meng Xun slept on the New Tower, eunuch Wang Huaizu struck him and wounded his foot; Meng Xun's wife Lady Meng seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜母車氏卒。

translations.literal: Meng Xun's mother, Lady Che, died.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun's mother, Lady Che, died.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙亥，魏主嗣如雲中舊宮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yihai, Wei ruler Si went to the old palace at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yihai, Wei Emperor Si went to the old palace at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 丙子，大赦。

translations.literal: On bingzi, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 西河胡張外等聚眾為盜；

translations.literal: Zhang Wai of the Xihe Hu and others gathered a band and became bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wai of the Xihe Hu and others raised a band of raiders;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，嗣遣會稽公長樂劉絜等屯西河招討之。

translations.literal: On yimao, Si sent the Duke of Kuaiji, Changle Liu Jie, and others to encamp in Xihe to recruit forces and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Si sent Duke of Kuaiji Changle Liu Jie and others to encamp in Xihe and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 六月，嗣如五原。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Si went to Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, he went to Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 朱齡石等至白帝發函書，曰：「眾軍悉從外水取成都。

translations.literal: Zhu Linshi and the others reached Baidi and opened the sealed dispatch, which read, "All armies shall take Chengdu by the outer water route.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Linshi and the others reached Baidi and opened the sealed orders: "All armies shall take Chengdu via the outer river.

sentences.zh: 臧熹從中水取廣漢，老弱乘高艦十餘，從內水向黃虎。」

translations.literal: Zang Xi shall take Guanghan by the middle water route; the old and weak shall board more than ten high ships and advance on Huanghu by the inner water route.」
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xi shall take Guanghan by the middle river; the aged and infirm shall board more than ten tall ships and move on Huanghu by the inner river."」

sentences.zh: 於是諸軍倍道兼行。

translations.literal: Thereupon the armies pressed forward at double speed.
translations.idiomatic: The armies then pressed forward at forced march.

sentences.zh: 譙縱果命譙道福將重兵鎮倍城，以備內水。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong indeed ordered Qiao Daofu to lead heavy troops to garrison Beicheng to guard against the inner water route.
translations.idiomatic: As expected, Qiao Zong ordered Qiao Daofu with a strong force to hold Beicheng against the inner river.

sentences.zh: 齡石至平模，去成都二百里，縱遣秦州刺史候暉、尚書僕射譙詵帥眾萬餘屯平模，夾岸築城以拒之。

translations.literal: Linshi reached Pingmo, two hundred li from Chengdu; Zong sent the Inspector of Qinzhou Hou Hui and the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Qiao Shen with more than ten thousand men to encamp at Pingmo, building walled camps on both banks of the river to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi reached Pingmo, two hundred li from Chengdu; Zong sent Qinzhou inspector Hou Hui and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Qiao Shen with more than ten thousand men to hold Pingmo, fortifying both banks of the river.

sentences.zh: 齡石謂劉鐘曰：「今天時盛熱，而賊嚴兵固險，攻之未必可拔，只增疲睏。

translations.literal: Linshi said to Liu Zhong, "Now the season is fiercely hot, and the enemy holds strong troops in entrenched positions; an attack may not succeed in taking them, and would only increase exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi said to Liu Zhong, "The weather is sweltering, the enemy holds strong positions behind ramparts—an assault may not succeed and will only wear our men down.

sentences.zh: 且欲養銳息兵以伺其隙，何如？」

translations.literal: Moreover, I wish to rest the sharp edge and give the troops ease to watch for an opening—what do you think?"」
translations.idiomatic: Would it not be better to rest our elite troops and wait for an opening?"」

sentences.zh: 鐘曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhong said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong replied, "I disagree.

sentences.zh: 前揚聲言大從向內水。

translations.literal: Previously we spread word that the main force would advance by the inner water route.
translations.idiomatic: We spread word that the main army would advance by the inner river.

sentences.zh: 譙道福不敢捨涪城。

translations.literal: Qiao Daofu did not dare leave Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Daofu dared not leave Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 今重軍猝至，出其不意，侯暉之徒已破膽矣。

translations.literal: Now our main army has arrived suddenly, catching them off guard; Hou Hui and his ilk have already lost their nerve.
translations.idiomatic: Now our main force has struck suddenly and caught them off guard—Hou Hui and his fellows are already terrified.

sentences.zh: 賊阻兵守險者，是其懼不敢戰也。

translations.literal: That the enemy blocks with troops and holds the passes shows they are afraid and dare not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Their blocking the passes with troops shows fear—they dare not give battle.

sentences.zh: 因其兇懼。

translations.literal: Take advantage of their fright and terror.
translations.idiomatic: Strike while they are shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 盡銳攻之，其勢必克。

translations.literal: Attack with all our elite strength, and the position will surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Throw our best troops against them and we shall certainly prevail.

sentences.zh: 克平模之後，自可鼓行而進，成都必不能守矣。

translations.literal: After taking Pingmo, we can march in confidence, and Chengdu will surely be unable to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Once Pingmo falls, we can advance in triumph and Chengdu cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 若緩兵相守，彼將知人虛實。

translations.literal: If we linger and hold a static defense, they will learn our true strength.
translations.idiomatic: If we delay and merely hold our positions, they will learn what we really have.

sentences.zh: 涪軍忽來，並力拒我。

translations.literal: The Fucheng army will suddenly arrive and join forces to resist us.
translations.idiomatic: The army at Fucheng will come up suddenly and oppose us in force.

sentences.zh: 人情既安，良將又集，此求戰不獲，軍食無資，二萬餘人悉為蜀子虜矣。」

translations.literal: Once the men's spirits settle and good generals gather, we will seek battle in vain, have no provisions, and more than twenty thousand men will all become captives of the Shu rebels.」
translations.idiomatic: Their spirits will recover, their best commanders will gather—then we shall find no battle, our supplies will fail, and more than twenty thousand men will become captives of Shu."」

sentences.zh: 齡石從之。

translations.literal: Linshi followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi agreed.

sentences.zh: 諸將以水北城地險兵多，欲先攻其南城。

translations.literal: The generals, because the northern city on the water's north side had perilous terrain and many troops, wished to attack the southern city first.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to attack the southern city first, since the northern city across the river had strong terrain and a large garrison.

sentences.zh: 齡石曰：「今屠南城，不足以破北，若盡銳以拔北城，則南城不麾自散矣。」

translations.literal: Linshi said, "Now if we slaughter our way through the southern city, it will not suffice to break the north; if we concentrate our elite to take the northern city, the southern city will disperse without a wave of the banner.」
translations.idiomatic: Linshi said, "Taking the southern city alone won't break them; if we concentrate our strength on the northern city, the southern one will collapse without a fight."」

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，齡石帥諸軍急攻北城，克之，斬侯暉、譙詵；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Linshi led the armies in a swift assault on the northern city, took it, and beheaded Hou Hui and Qiao Shen;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Linshi led a furious assault on the northern city, took it, and beheaded Hou Hui and Qiao Shen;

sentences.zh: 引兵回趣南城，南城自潰。

translations.literal: He led his troops back to rush the southern city, and the southern city collapsed on its own.
translations.idiomatic: He wheeled about against the southern city, which collapsed without a fight.

sentences.zh: 齡石捨船步進。

translations.literal: Linshi abandoned the ships and advanced on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi abandoned the boats and marched overland.

sentences.zh: 焦縱大將譙撫之屯牛脾，譙小苟塞打鼻。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong's great general Qiao Fuzhi encamped at Niupi; Qiao Xiaogou blocked Dani.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong's general Qiao Fuzhi held Niupi; Qiao Xiaogou blocked Dani.

sentences.zh: 臧熹擊撫之，斬之；

translations.literal: Zang Xi attacked Fuzhi and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xi attacked Fuzhi and killed him;

sentences.zh: 小苟聞之，亦潰。

translations.literal: When Xiaogou heard of it, he too collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaogou heard of it, his force collapsed as well.

sentences.zh: 於是縱諸營屯望風相次奔潰。

translations.literal: Thereupon all of Zong's garrison camps fled and collapsed one after another at the sight of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Qiao Zong's camps collapsed in succession, each fleeing at the first sign of defeat.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，縱棄成都出走，尚書令馬耽封府庫以待晉師。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Zong abandoned Chengdu and fled; Director of the Masters of Writing Ma Dan sealed the treasury to await the Jin army.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Qiao Zong abandoned Chengdu and fled; Director of the Masters of Writing Ma Dan sealed the treasury to await the Jin forces.

sentences.zh: 壬申，齡石入成都，誅縱同祖之親，餘皆按堵，使復其業。

translations.literal: On renshen, Linshi entered Chengdu, executed Zong's relatives of the same ancestral line, and for the rest restored order so they could resume their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Linshi entered Chengdu, executed Qiao Zong's clan kin, and let the rest return peacefully to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 縱出成都。

translations.literal: Zong departed Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong left Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 先辭墓，其女曰：「走必不免，只取辱焉。

translations.literal: First he took leave at the ancestral tombs; his daughter said, "Flight cannot avoid capture—it will only bring disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he visited the family tombs; his daughter said, "Flight cannot save you—it will only bring shame.

sentences.zh: 等死，死於先人之墓可也。」

translations.literal: If death is the same either way, dying at the tombs of our ancestors would be fitting.」
translations.idiomatic: Death is death either way—better to die at our ancestors' graves."」

sentences.zh: 縱不從。

translations.literal: Zong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong refused.

sentences.zh: 譙道福聞平模不守。

translations.literal: Qiao Daofu heard that Pingmo was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Daofu learned that Pingmo had fallen.

sentences.zh: 自涪引兵入赴，縱往投之。

translations.literal: He led troops from Fu to march in relief; Zong went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched from Fu to reinforce the position; Qiao Zong fled to join him.

sentences.zh: 道福見縱，怒曰：「大丈夫有如此功業而棄之，將安歸乎！

translations.literal: Daofu saw Zong and angrily said, "A true man with such achievements—where will you go if you cast them away!
translations.idiomatic: Daofu saw him and raged: "A man who built an empire like this—where do you think you can go by throwing it away!

sentences.zh: 人誰不死，何怯之甚也！」

translations.literal: Who among men does not die—why this extreme cowardice!」
translations.idiomatic: Every man must die—why this spineless terror!"」

sentences.zh: 因投縱以劍，中其馬鞍。

translations.literal: He then threw his sword at Zong and struck his saddle.
translations.idiomatic: He flung his sword at Qiao Zong and struck his saddle.

sentences.zh: 縱乃去，自縊死，巴西人王志斬其首以送齡石。

translations.literal: Zong then departed, hanged himself, and the man of Baxi Wang Zhi cut off his head and sent it to Linshi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong rode away and hanged himself; Wang Zhi of Baxi cut off his head and sent it to Linshi.

sentences.zh: 道福謂其眾曰：「蜀之存亡，實繫於我，不在譙王。

translations.literal: Daofu said to his troops, "Whether Shu lives or dies depends on me—not on the Prince of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu told his troops, "Shu's fate rests with me, not with the Prince of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 今我在，猶足一戰。」

translations.literal: As long as I am here, we still have strength for one battle.」
translations.idiomatic: While I remain, we can still fight one more battle."」

sentences.zh: 眾皆許諾。

translations.literal: All pledged their assent.
translations.idiomatic: They all assented.

sentences.zh: 道福盡散金帛以賜眾，眾受之而走。

translations.literal: Daofu distributed all his gold and silk to reward the troops; they accepted it and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu gave away all his gold and silk to the troops; they took the gifts and ran.

sentences.zh: 道福逃於獠中，巴民杜瑾執送之，斬於軍門。

translations.literal: Daofu fled among the Liao tribes; the man of Ba Du Jin seized and sent him; he was beheaded at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu fled among the Liao tribes; Du Jin of Ba captured him and handed him over, and he was beheaded before the camp.

sentences.zh: 齡石徙馬耽於越嵩，耽謂其徒曰：「朱侯不送我京師，欲滅口也，吾必不免。」

translations.literal: Linshi relocated Ma Dan to Yuexi; Dan said to his followers, "Marquis Zhu does not send me to the capital but wants to seal my mouth—I cannot escape death.」
translations.idiomatic: Linshi exiled Ma Dan to Yuexi; Dan told his followers, "Marquis Zhu is not sending me to the capital—he means to silence me. I cannot escape."」

sentences.zh: 乃盥洗而臥，引繩而死。

translations.literal: He then washed, lay down, and died by hanging himself with a rope.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed, lay down, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 須臾，齡石使至，戮其屍。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Linshi's envoy arrived and mutilated his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later Linshi's messenger arrived and desecrated the body.

sentences.zh: 詔以齡石進監梁、秦州六郡諸軍事，賜爵豐城縣侯。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Linshi to supervise military affairs of the six commanderies of Liang and Qin, and bestowed the title Marquis of Fengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Linshi supervisor of military affairs in the six Liang and Qin commanderies and created him Marquis of Fengcheng County.

sentences.zh: 魏奚斤等破越勤於跋那山西，徙二萬餘家於大寧。

translations.literal: Wei forces under Xi Jin and others defeated the Yueqin west of Bana Mountain and relocated more than twenty thousand households to Dading.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin and other Wei commanders defeated the Yueqin west of Bana Mountain and resettled more than twenty thousand households at Dading.

sentences.zh: 河西胡曹龍等擁部眾二萬人來入蒲子，張外降之，推龍為大單于。

translations.literal: Cao Long of the Hexi Hu and others, leading a following of twenty thousand men, entered Puzi; Zhang Wai submitted to them and made Long Great Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Long of the Hexi Hu entered Puzi at the head of twenty thousand followers; Zhang Wai submitted and proclaimed him Great Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，魏主嗣如定襄大洛城。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Wei ruler Si went to Dingxiang's Daluo City.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Wei Emperor Si went to Daluo City in Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 河南王熾磐擊吐谷渾支旁於長柳川，虜旁及其民五千餘戶而還。

translations.literal: The Prince of Henan, Qifu Chifen, attacked the Tuyuhun Zhi Pang at Changliu River, captured Pang and more than five thousand of his people, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Henan Qifu Chifen attacked the Tuyuhun Zhi Pang at Changliu River, took him and more than five thousand of his people captive, and returned.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸卯，魏主嗣還平城。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guimao, Wei ruler Si returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guimao, Wei Emperor Si returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 曹龍請降魏，執送張外，斬之。

translations.literal: Cao Long requested to submit to Wei, seized and sent Zhang Wai, and had him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Long offered to submit to Wei, delivered Zhang Wai in chains, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，魏主嗣如豺山宮。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Wei ruler Si went to the Mount Chai Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Wei Emperor Si went to Mount Chai Palace.

sentences.zh: 癸未，還。

translations.literal: On guiwei, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, he returned.

sentences.zh: 九月，再命太尉裕為太傅、揚州牧；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Yu was again appointed Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Liu Yu was again appointed Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou;

sentences.zh: 固辭。

translations.literal: He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He declined again.

sentences.zh: 河南王熾磐擊吐谷渾別統掘逵於渴渾川，大破之，虜男女二萬三千。

translations.literal: The Prince of Henan, Qifu Chifen, attacked the Tuyuhun sub-commander Ju Kui at Kehun River, utterly defeated him, and captured twenty-three thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Henan Qifu Chifen routed the Tuyuhun sub-commander Ju Kui at Kehun River and took twenty-three thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，掘逵帥其餘眾降於熾磐。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Ju Kui led his remaining followers and submitted to Chifen.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Ju Kui surrendered with his remaining force to Chifen.

sentences.zh: 吐京胡與離石胡出以眷叛魏，魏主嗣命元城侯屈督會稽公劉暠、永安侯魏勤以討之。

translations.literal: The Tujing Hu and the Lishi Hu Chu Yijuan rebelled against Wei; Wei ruler Si ordered the Marquis of Yuancheng Qu to supervise the Duke of Kuaiji Liu Hao and the Marquis of Yong'an Wei Qin to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tujing and Lishi Hu under Chu Yijuan rebelled against Wei; Emperor Si ordered Marquis of Yuancheng Qu to lead Duke of Kuaiji Liu Hao and Marquis of Yong'an Wei Qin against them.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，出以眷引夏兵邀擊暠，禽之，以獻於夏；

translations.literal: On dingsi, Chu Yijuan led Xia troops to intercept and attack Hao, captured him, and presented him to Xia;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Chu Yijuan led Xia forces to ambush Liu Hao, captured him, and sent him to Xia;

sentences.zh: 勤戰死。

translations.literal: Qin died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qin died in battle.

sentences.zh: 嗣以屈亡二將，欲誅之；

translations.literal: Si because Qu had lost two generals wished to execute him;
translations.idiomatic: Because Qu had lost two generals, Emperor Si wanted to put him to death;

sentences.zh: 既而赦之，使攝并州刺史。

translations.literal: soon after pardoned him and had him act as Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: he soon pardoned him instead and appointed him acting Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 屈到州，縱酒廢事，嗣積其前後罪惡，檻車征還。

translations.literal: When Qu reached the province he indulged in wine and neglected affairs; Si accumulated his past and present crimes and summoned him back in a prisoner cart.
translations.idiomatic: When Qu reached his post he drank to excess and neglected his duties; Emperor Si tallied his old and new offenses and had him brought back in a caged cart.

sentences.zh: 斬之。

translations.literal: He was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Qu was executed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏主嗣遣使請昏於秦，秦王興許之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wei ruler Si sent envoys to request a marriage alliance with Qin; King Yao Xing of Qin agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Wei Emperor Si sent envoys to seek a marriage alliance with Qin, and King Yao Xing agreed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以敦煌索邈為梁州刺史，苻宣乃還仇池。

translations.literal: That year Suo Miao of Dunhuang was made Inspector of Liangzhou, and Fu Xuan then returned to Chouci.
translations.idiomatic: That year Suo Miao of Dunhuang was appointed Inspector of Liangzhou, and Fu Xuan returned to Chouci.

sentences.zh: 初，邈寓居漢川，與別駕姜顯有隙，凡十五年而邈鎮漢川；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Miao had lived as a guest in Hanchuan, he had a rift with Chief Assistant Jiang Xian; fifteen years passed before Miao governed Hanchuan;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while living in Hanchuan as a guest, Miao had quarreled with Chief Assistant Jiang Xian; fifteen years passed before Miao was posted to govern Hanchuan;

sentences.zh: 顯乃肉袒迎候，邈無慍色，待之彌厚。

translations.literal: Xian then bared his torso to welcome him; Miao showed no anger and treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Xian came out bare-chested to receive him; Miao showed no resentment and treated him even more warmly.

sentences.zh: 退而謂人曰：「我昔寓此，失志多年，若仇姜顯，懼者不少。

translations.literal: Withdrawn, he said to others, "When I once lived here as a guest, I was frustrated for many years; if I had treated Jiang Xian as an enemy, many would have been afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he told others, "When I lived here in exile, I was frustrated for many years; had I nursed a grudge against Jiang Xian, many would have lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 但服之自佳，何必逞志！」

translations.literal: Simply yielding to him is best in itself—why must one indulge one's will!"
translations.idiomatic: Simply yielding to him is its own reward—why indulge one's pride!"

sentences.zh: 於是闔境聞之皆悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon all within the circuit who heard of it were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When word of this spread through the circuit, all were pleased.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝辛義熙十年（

translations.literal: Emperor An, Xin, tenth year of Yixi (
translations.idiomatic: The tenth year of Yixi of Emperor An (

sentences.zh: 甲寅，公元四一四年）

translations.literal: jiayin, the year 414 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiayin, 414 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉，魏大赦，改元神瑞。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinyou, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yuansui.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the xinyou day of the first month, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yuansui.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，魏主嗣如繁畤。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Wei ruler Si went to Fanchi.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Wei Emperor Si went to Fanchi.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊戌，還平城。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuxu, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuxu, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃侵魏河東蒲子。

translations.literal: Xia King Heluobobo invaded Puzi in Wei's Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xia King Heluobobo invaded Puzi in Wei's Hedong command.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏主嗣如豺山宮。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Wei ruler Si went to Mount Chai Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Wei Emperor Si went to Mount Chai Palace.

sentences.zh: 魏并州刺史婁伏連襲殺夏所置吐京護軍及其守兵。

translations.literal: Wei Inspector of Bingzhou Lou Fulian made a surprise attack and killed the Protector of the Army that Xia had installed at Tujing and his garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Fulian, Inspector of Bingzhou for Wei, raided and killed the Protector of the Army Xia had posted at Tujing along with the garrison.

sentences.zh: 司馬休之在江陵，頗得江、漢民心。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi was at Jiangling and had won considerable favor among the people of the Jiang and Han regions.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi was at Jiangling and had won considerable goodwill among the people of the Jiang and Han regions.

sentences.zh: 子譙王文思在建康，性凶暴，好通輕俠；

translations.literal: His son Wensi, Prince of Qiao, was in Jiankang—violent by nature and fond of consorting with reckless swordsmen;
translations.idiomatic: His son Wensi, Prince of Qiao, was in Jiankang—violent by nature and fond of reckless company;

sentences.zh: 太尉裕惡之。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yu detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Liu Yu detested him.

sentences.zh: 三月，有司奏文思擅捶殺國吏，詔誅其黨而宥文思。

translations.literal: In the third month the responsible officials reported that Wensi had beaten and killed a state official on his own authority; an edict ordered his followers executed while pardoning Wensi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the authorities reported that Wensi had beaten a state official to death on his own authority; an edict ordered his followers executed while sparing Wensi himself.

sentences.zh: 休之上疏謝罪，請解所任；

translations.literal: Xiuzhi submitted a memorial apologizing and asking to be relieved of his post;
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi submitted a memorial apologizing and asking to be relieved of his duties;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 裕執文思送休之，令自訓厲，意欲休之殺之；

translations.literal: Yu seized Wensi and sent him to Xiuzhi, ordering him to discipline the boy himself—Yu's intent was that Xiuzhi would kill him;
translations.idiomatic: Yu seized Wensi and sent him to Xiuzhi with orders to discipline him himself, hoping Xiuzhi would kill him;

sentences.zh: 休之但表廢文思。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi merely memorialized to disinherit Wensi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi merely memorialized to disinherit Wensi.

sentences.zh: 並與裕書陳謝。

translations.literal: He also wrote Yu a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Liu Yu a letter of apology.

sentences.zh: 裕由是不悅，以江州刺史孟懷玉兼督豫州六郡以備之。

translations.literal: Yu was displeased by this and made Jiangzhou Inspector Meng Huaiyu concurrently oversee the six commanderies of Yuzhou as a precaution against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was displeased and made Jiangzhou Inspector Meng Huaiyu concurrently oversee the six commanderies of Yuzhou to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，辛酉，魏主嗣還平城。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on xinyou, Wei ruler Si returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the xinyou day of the fifth month, Wei Emperor Si returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 秦後將軍斂成討叛羌，為羌所敗，懼罪，出奔夏。

translations.literal: Qin Rear General Yang Cheng campaigned against rebellious Qiang, was defeated by the Qiang, feared punishment, and fled to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Rear General Yang Cheng campaigned against rebellious Qiang, was defeated, feared punishment, and fled to Xia.

sentences.zh: 秦王興有疾，妖賊李弘與氐仇常反於貳城，興輿疾往討之，斬常，執弘而還。

translations.literal: King Yao Xing of Qin was ill; the sorcerer-rebel Li Hong and the Di Chou Chang rebelled at Ercheng; Xing went to suppress them despite his illness, beheaded Chang, captured Hong, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: King Yao Xing was ill when the sorcerer-rebel Li Hong and the Di Chou Chang rose at Ercheng; Xing went to suppress them despite his illness, beheaded Chang, captured Hong, and returned.

sentences.zh: 秦左將軍姚文宗有寵於太子泓，廣平公弼惡之，誣文宗有怨言；

translations.literal: Qin Left General Yao Wenzong enjoyed the favor of Crown Prince Hong; Guangping Duke Bi hated him and falsely accused Wenzong of discontent;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Left General Yao Wenzong enjoyed Crown Prince Hong's favor; Guangping Duke Bi hated him and falsely accused Wenzong of disloyal complaints;

sentences.zh: 秦王興怒，賜文宗死，於是群臣畏弼側目。

translations.literal: King Yao Xing was angry and ordered Wenzong to die; thereafter the ministers feared Bi and looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: King Yao Xing was enraged and ordered Wenzong to take his own life; from then on the ministers feared Bi and looked on him with dread.

sentences.zh: 弼言於興，無不從者；

translations.literal: Whatever Bi said to Xing, Xing never refused;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Bi said to Yao Xing, Yao Xing never refused;

sentences.zh: 以所親天水尹沖為給事黃門侍郎，唐盛為治書侍御史，興左右掌機要者，皆其黨也。

translations.literal: he appointed his intimates Yin Chong of Tianshui as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Tang Sheng as Imperial Secretary; those around Xing who controlled vital affairs were all his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: he made his intimates Yin Chong of Tianshui Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Tang Sheng Imperial Secretary, and all those around Yao Xing who controlled vital affairs were his partisans.

sentences.zh: 右僕射梁喜、侍中任廉、亦兆尹尹昭承間言於興曰：「父子之際，人所難言；

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Liang Xi, Attendant-in-Ordinary Ren Lian, and Capital Intendant Yin Zhao seized an opportunity to speak to Xing, saying, "Between father and son there are things men find hard to say;
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Liang Xi, Attendant-in-Ordinary Ren Lian, and Capital Intendant Yin Zhao seized an opportunity to speak to Yao Xing, saying, "Between father and son there are things men hesitate to say;

sentences.zh: 然君臣之義，不薄於父子，故臣等不得默然。

translations.literal: yet the duty between ruler and minister is no lighter than that between father and son, so we cannot remain silent.
translations.idiomatic: yet the bond between ruler and minister is no less weighty than that between father and son, so we cannot remain silent.

sentences.zh: 廣平公弼，潛有奪嫡之志，陛下寵之太過，假其威權，傾險無賴之徒輻湊附之。

translations.literal: Guangping Duke Bi secretly harbors the ambition to seize the succession; Your Majesty favors him excessively and lends him authority and power, and scheming, unscrupulous men flock to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangping Duke Bi secretly harbors the ambition to supplant the heir; Your Majesty favors him too much, lends him power, and scheming ruffians flock to his side.

sentences.zh: 道路皆言陛下將有廢立之計，信有之乎！」

translations.literal: The roads are full of talk that Your Majesty intends a deposition and installation—is this true!"
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere people say Your Majesty plans to depose the crown prince and install another—is there truth in this?"

sentences.zh: 興曰：「豈有此邪！」

translations.literal: Xing said, "How could there be such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing said, "How could there be such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 喜等曰：「苟無之，則陛下愛弼，適所以禍之；

translations.literal: Xi and the others said, "If there is none, then Your Majesty's love for Bi is precisely what will bring disaster upon him;
translations.idiomatic: Xi and the others said, "If there is no such plan, then Your Majesty's affection for Bi is precisely what will ruin him;

sentences.zh: 願去其左右，損其威權，如此，非特安弼，乃所以安宗廟社稷。」

translations.literal: We ask that you remove those at his side and reduce his authority and power; in this way you will not only secure Bi but also secure the ancestral temple and the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that you remove his followers and curb his power; in that way you will not only protect Bi but also secure the ancestral temple and the state."

sentences.zh: 興不應。

translations.literal: Xing did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing did not answer.

sentences.zh: 大司農竇溫、司徒左長史王弼皆密疏勸興立弼為太子，興雖不從，亦不責也。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture Dou Wen and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works Wang Bi both sent secret memorials urging Xing to make Bi crown prince; though Xing did not agree, he did not rebuke them either.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Agriculture Dou Wen and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works Wang Bi both sent secret memorials urging Yao Xing to make Bi crown prince; though he did not agree, he did not rebuke them either.

sentences.zh: 興疾篤，弼潛聚眾數千人，謀作亂。

translations.literal: When Xing's illness grew grave, Bi secretly gathered several thousand men and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing's illness grew grave, Bi secretly gathered several thousand men and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 姚裕遣使以弼逆狀告諸兄在籓鎮者，於是姚懿治兵於蒲孤，鎮東將軍、豫州牧洸治兵於洛陽，平西將軍諶治兵於雍，皆欲赴長安討弼。

translations.literal: Yao Yu sent messengers to report Bi's treason to his brothers stationed in frontier commands; thereupon Yao Yi marshaled troops at Pugu, Area Commander of the East and Governor of Yuzhou Guang marshaled troops at Luoyang, and General Who Pacifies the West Chen marshaled troops at Yong—all intending to march on Chang'an to punish Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yu sent messengers to report Bi's treason to his brothers in the frontier commands; Yao Yi then marshaled troops at Pugu, Area Commander of the East and Governor of Yuzhou Guang did the same at Luoyang, and General Who Pacifies the West Chen at Yong—all intending to march on Chang'an to punish Bi.

sentences.zh: 會興疾瘳，見群臣，征虜將軍劉羌泣以告興。

translations.literal: It happened that Xing's illness improved; when he received the ministers, General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians Liu Qiang wept as he reported to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yao Xing recovered; when he received the ministers, General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians Liu Qiang wept as he told Yao Xing what had happened.

sentences.zh: 梁喜、尹昭請誅弼，且曰：「苟陛下不忍殺弼，亦當奪其權任。」

translations.literal: Liang Xi and Yin Zhao asked that Bi be executed, adding, "If Your Majesty cannot bear to kill Bi, you should at least strip him of his authority and office."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi and Yin Zhao asked that Bi be executed, adding, "If Your Majesty cannot bear to kill Bi, you should at least strip him of his authority and office."

sentences.zh: 興不得已，免弼尚書令，使以將軍、公還第。

translations.literal: Xing had no choice; he removed Bi as Director of the Masters of Writing and sent him home with only his titles as general and duke.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing had no choice; he removed Bi as Director of the Masters of Writing and sent him home retaining only his titles as general and duke.

sentences.zh: 懿等各罷兵。

translations.literal: Yi and the others each disbanded their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others each disbanded their armies.

sentences.zh: 懿、洸、諶與姚宣皆入朝，使裕入白興，求見，興曰：「汝等正欲論弼事耳，吾已知之。」

translations.literal: Yi, Guang, Chen, and Yao Xuan all entered court; Yao Yu went in to inform Xing and request an audience; Xing said, "You wish only to discuss Bi's affair—I already know of it."
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Guang, Chen, and Yao Xuan all entered court; Yao Yu went in to inform Yao Xing and request an audience; Yao Xing said, "You wish only to discuss Bi's affair—I already know of it."

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「弼苟有可論，陛下所宜垂聽；

translations.literal: Yu said, "If Bi's case merits discussion, Your Majesty ought to hear it;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yu said, "If Bi's case merits discussion, Your Majesty ought to hear it;

sentences.zh: 若懿等言非是，便當置之刑辟，奈何逆抿之！」

translations.literal: if what Yi and the others say is wrong, they should be brought to justice—why dismiss them out of hand!"
translations.idiomatic: if what Yi and the others say is false, they should be punished by law—why reject them out of hand!"

sentences.zh: 於是引見懿等於諮議堂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he received Yi and the others at the Hall of Consultation.
translations.idiomatic: He then received Yi and the others at the Hall of Consultation.

sentences.zh: 宣流涕極言，興曰：「吾自處之，非汝曹所憂。」

translations.literal: Xuan wept as he spoke at length; Xing said, "I shall handle this myself—it is not for you to worry."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wept as he spoke at length; Yao Xing said, "I shall handle this myself—it is not for you to worry."

sentences.zh: 撫軍東曹屬姜虯上疏曰：「廣平公弼，釁成逆著，道路皆知之。

translations.literal: Adjutant of the Eastern Staff of the Pacification Army Jiang Qiu submitted a memorial saying, "Guangping Duke Bi's guilt for rebellion is already evident, and everyone on the roads knows it.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant of the Eastern Staff of the Pacification Army Jiang Qiu submitted a memorial saying, "Guangping Duke Bi's guilt for rebellion is already plain, and everyone knows it.

sentences.zh: 昔文王之化，刑於寡妻；

translations.literal: In antiquity King Wen's transforming influence began with his wife;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity King Wen's transforming virtue began with his own household;

sentences.zh: 今聖朝之亂，起自愛子，雖欲含忍掩蔽，而逆黨扇惑不已，弼之亂心何由可革！

translations.literal: today the disorder of the sacred court arises from a beloved son; though one wishes to forbear and conceal it, the rebellious faction keeps inciting unrest—how can Bi's rebellious heart be reformed!
translations.idiomatic: today the court's disorder springs from a beloved son; though you wish to forbear and conceal it, the rebellious faction keeps stirring trouble—how can Bi's rebellious heart be changed!

sentences.zh: 宜斥散兇徒，以絕禍端。」

translations.literal: You should disperse the violent followers to cut off the source of disaster."
translations.idiomatic: You should disperse his violent followers to cut off the source of disaster."

sentences.zh: 興以虯表示梁喜曰：「天下人皆以吾兒為口實，將何以處之？」

translations.literal: Xing showed Qiu's memorial to Liang Xi and said, "All under heaven use my son as a topic of gossip—how am I to deal with this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing showed Qiu's memorial to Liang Xi and said, "All under heaven use my son as gossip—how am I to deal with this?"

sentences.zh: 喜曰：「信如虯言，陛下早宜裁決。」

translations.literal: Xi said, "If Qiu's words are true, Your Majesty should decide early."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "If Qiu's words are true, Your Majesty should decide at once."

sentences.zh: 興默然。

translations.literal: Xing was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing fell silent.

sentences.zh: 唾契汗、乙弗等部皆叛南涼，南涼王辱檀欲討之，邯川護軍孟愷諫曰：「今連年饑饉，南逼熾磐，北逼蒙遜，百姓不安。

translations.literal: The Tuoqihan, Yifu, and other tribes all rebelled against Southern Liang; Tufa Rutan, King of Southern Liang, wished to suppress them; Hanchuan Protector of the Army Meng Kai remonstrated, saying, "For years now there has been famine; to the south Chibpan presses us, to the north Mengxun presses us, and the people are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuoqihan, Yifu, and other tribes all rebelled against Southern Liang; Tufa Rutan wished to suppress them; Hanchuan Protector of the Army Meng Kai remonstrated, saying, "Famine has continued for years; Chibpan presses us from the south and Mengxun from the north, and the people are unsettled.

sentences.zh: 遠征雖克，必有後患；

translations.literal: Though a distant campaign may succeed, there will surely be trouble afterward;
translations.idiomatic: Even if a distant campaign succeeds, trouble will follow;

sentences.zh: 不如與熾磐結盟通糴，慰撫雜部，足食繕兵，俟時而動。」

translations.literal: it would be better to ally with Chibpan and trade grain, reassure the various tribes, fill the granaries and repair the arms, and wait for the right moment to act."
translations.idiomatic: it would be better to ally with Chibpan and trade grain, reassure the various tribes, fill the granaries and repair arms, and wait for the right moment."

sentences.zh: 辱檀不從，謂太子虎台曰：「蒙遜近去，不能猝來，旦夕所慮，唯在熾磐。

translations.literal: Rutan would not listen and said to Crown Prince Hutai, "Mengxun has just withdrawn and cannot come suddenly; the only worry day and night is Chibpan.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan would not listen and told Crown Prince Hutai, "Mengxun has just withdrawn and cannot come at once; day and night the only worry is Chibpan.

sentences.zh: 然熾磐兵少易御，汝謹守樂都，吾不過一月必還矣。」

translations.literal: Yet Chibpan's forces are few and easy to handle; you guard Ledu carefully—I shall return within a month at most."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chibpan's forces are few and easy to handle; guard Ledu carefully—I shall return within a month at most."

sentences.zh: 乃帥騎七千襲乙弗，大破之，獲馬牛羊四十餘萬。

translations.literal: He then led seven thousand cavalry in a surprise attack on the Yifu, routed them utterly, and captured more than four hundred thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: He then led seven thousand cavalry against the Yifu, routed them, and captured more than four hundred thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 河南王熾磐聞之，欲襲東都。

translations.literal: Prince of Henan Qifu Chibpan heard of this and wished to strike the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Henan Qifu Chibpan heard of this and wished to strike Ledu.

sentences.zh: 群臣鹹以為不可。

translations.literal: The ministers all thought it inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all thought it inadvisable.

sentences.zh: 太府主簿焦襲曰：「辱檀不顧近患而貪遠利，我今伐之，絕其西路，使不得還救。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Grand Treasury Jiao Xi said, "Rutan ignores the danger close at hand and covets distant gain; if we attack him now and cut off his western route so that he cannot return to the rescue,
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk of the Grand Treasury Jiao Xi said, "Rutan ignores nearby danger to chase distant gain; if we attack now and cut off his western route so he cannot return to the rescue,

sentences.zh: 則虎台獨守窮城，可坐禽也。

translations.literal: then Hutai will be left alone defending a desperate city, and we can capture him without effort.
translations.idiomatic: Hutai will be left alone in a desperate city, and we can take him without effort.

sentences.zh: 此天亡之時，必不可失。」

translations.literal: This is the hour Heaven has ordained his destruction—it must not be missed."
translations.idiomatic: This is the hour Heaven has ordained his destruction—it must not be missed."

sentences.zh: 熾磐從之，帥步騎二萬襲樂都。

translations.literal: Chibpan agreed and led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry in a surprise attack on Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Chibpan agreed and led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry against Ledu.

sentences.zh: 虎台憑城拒守，熾磐四面攻之。

translations.literal: Hutai relied on the walls to resist; Chibpan attacked from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Hutai held the walls and resisted; Chibpan attacked from all four sides.

sentences.zh: 南涼撫軍從事中郎尉肅言於虎台曰：「外城廣大難守，殿下不若聚國人守內城，肅等帥晉人拒戰於外，雖有不捷，猶足自存。」

translations.literal: Adjutant of the Pacification Army Wei Su of Southern Liang said to Hutai, "The outer city is vast and hard to defend; Your Highness would do better to gather our own people to hold the inner city while Su and the others lead the Jin men to fight outside; even if we do not prevail, we can still preserve ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant of the Pacification Army Wei Su said to Hutai, "The outer city is vast and hard to defend; Your Highness would do better to gather our own people in the inner city while we lead the Jin men to fight outside; even if we fail, we can still survive."

sentences.zh: 虎台曰：「熾磐小賊，旦夕當走，卿何過慮之深！」

translations.literal: Hutai said, "Chibpan is a petty bandit who will flee before long—why do you worry so much!"
translations.idiomatic: Hutai said, "Chibpan is a petty bandit who will flee before long—why worry so much!"

sentences.zh: 虎台疑晉人有異心，悉召豪望有謀勇者閉之於內。

translations.literal: Hutai suspected the Jin men of disloyalty and summoned all the leading men of courage and counsel, shutting them inside.
translations.idiomatic: Hutai suspected the Jin men of disloyalty and summoned all the leading men of courage and counsel, shutting them inside.

sentences.zh: 孟愷泣曰：「熾磐乘虛內侮，國家危於累卵。

translations.literal: Meng Kai wept and said, "Chibpan is seizing our weakness to attack us within—the state is in danger as precarious as a pile of eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Kai wept and said, "Chibpan is exploiting our weakness to strike within—the state hangs by a thread.

sentences.zh: 愷等進欲報恩，退顧妻子，人思效死，而殿下乃疑之如是邪！」

translations.literal: We wish to advance and repay our debt of gratitude, and when we withdraw we think of our wives and children—every man is ready to die for the cause, yet Your Highness suspects us like this!"
translations.idiomatic: We wish to advance and repay our debt, and when we withdraw we think of our families—every man is ready to die for the cause, yet Your Highness suspects us like this!"

sentences.zh: 虎台曰：「吾豈不知君之忠篤，懼餘人脫生慮表，以君等安之耳。」

translations.literal: Hutai said, "Do you think I do not know your loyalty and devotion? I feared that if the others were released they might show signs of wavering—I kept you here only to reassure you."
translations.idiomatic: Hutai said, "Do you think I do not know your loyalty? I feared that if the others were released they might show signs of wavering—I kept you here only to reassure you."

sentences.zh: 一夕，城潰，熾磐入樂都，遣平遠將軍捷虔帥騎五千追辱檀，以鎮南將軍廉屯為都督河右諸軍事、涼州刺史，鎮樂都；

translations.literal: One night the walls collapsed; Chibpan entered Ledu, sent General Who Pacifies the Distance Jie Qian with five thousand cavalry in pursuit of Rutan, and made General Who Guards the South Lian Tun Area Commander of military affairs west of the Yellow River and Inspector of Liangzhou, stationed at Ledu;
translations.idiomatic: One night the walls gave way; Chibpan entered Ledu, sent General Who Pacifies the Distance Jie Qian with five thousand cavalry in pursuit of Rutan, and made General Who Guards the South Lian Tun Area Commander of military affairs west of the Yellow River and Inspector of Liangzhou, stationed at Ledu;

sentences.zh: 禿髮赴單為西平太守，鎮西平；

translations.literal: Tufa Fudan was made Administrator of Xiping and garrisoned Xiping;
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Fudan was made Administrator of Xiping and garrisoned Xiping;

sentences.zh: 以趙恢為廣武太守，鎮廣武；

translations.literal: Zhao Hui was made Administrator of Guangwu and garrisoned Guangwu;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hui was made Administrator of Guangwu and garrisoned Guangwu;

sentences.zh: 曜武將軍王基為晉興太守，鎮浩亹；

translations.literal: General Who Displays Martiality Wang Ji was made Administrator of Jinxing and garrisoned Hao'e;
translations.idiomatic: General Who Displays Martiality Wang Ji was made Administrator of Jinxing and garrisoned Hao'e;

sentences.zh: 徙虎台及其文武百姓萬餘戶於枹罕。

translations.literal: Hutai and more than ten thousand households of officials, soldiers, and common people were moved to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Hutai and more than ten thousand households of officials, soldiers, and commoners were relocated to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 赴單，烏孤之子也。

translations.literal: Fudan was a son of Tufa Wugu.
translations.idiomatic: Fudan was a son of Tufa Wugu.

sentences.zh: 河間人褚匡言於燕王跋曰：「陛下龍飛遼、碣，舊邦族黨，傾首朝陽，以日為歲，請往迎之。」

translations.literal: Chu Kuang of Hejian said to King Ba of Yan, "Your Majesty rose like a dragon in Liaodong and Jieshi; the clansmen of our old homeland crane their necks toward the dawn and count days as years—I ask leave to go and welcome them."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Kuang of Hejian said to King Ba of Yan, "Your Majesty rose to power in Liaodong and Jieshi; the clansmen of our old homeland crane their necks toward the dawn and count days as years—I ask leave to go and welcome them."

sentences.zh: 跋曰：「道路數千里，復隔異國，如何可致？」

translations.literal: Ba said, "The road is several thousand li, and a foreign state lies between—how can they be brought here?"
translations.idiomatic: Ba said, "The road is several thousand li, and foreign lands lie between—how can they be brought here?"

sentences.zh: 匡曰：「章武臨海，舟楫可通，出於遼西臨渝，不為難也。」

translations.literal: Kuang said, "Zhangwu faces the sea and boats can reach it; setting out from Linyu in Liaoxi, it would not be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang said, "Zhangwu faces the sea and boats can reach it; setting out from Linyu in Liaoxi, it would not be difficult."

sentences.zh: 跋許之，以匡為游擊將軍、中書待郎，厚資遣之。

translations.literal: Ba agreed, made Kuang General of Mobile Command and Attendant Secretary of the Secretariat, gave him generous supplies, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Ba agreed, made Kuang General of Mobile Command and Attendant Secretary of the Secretariat, gave him generous supplies, and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 匡與跋從兄買、從弟睹自長樂帥五千餘戶歸於和龍，契丹、庫莫奚皆降於燕。

translations.literal: Kuang, together with Ba's older cousin Mai and younger cousin Du, led more than five thousand households from Changle back to Helong; the Khitan and Kumo Xi all submitted to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang, together with Ba's older cousin Mai and younger cousin Du, led more than five thousand households from Changle back to Helong; the Khitan and Kumo Xi all submitted to Yan.

sentences.zh: 跋署其大人為歸善王。

translations.literal: Ba appointed their chieftains Kings Who Return to Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Ba appointed their chieftains Kings Who Return to Goodness.

sentences.zh: 跋弟不避亂在高句麗，跋召之，以為左僕射，封常山公。

translations.literal: Ba's younger brother Bu, who had fled the turmoil in Goguryeo, was summoned by Ba, made Left Vice Director, and enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Ba's younger brother Bu, who had fled the turmoil to Goguryeo, was summoned by Ba, made Left Vice Director, and enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 柔然可汗斛津將嫁女於燕，斛律兄子步鹿真謂斛律曰：「幼女遠嫁憂思，請以大臣樹黎等女為媵。」

translations.literal: Rouran Khagan Hulu was about to marry his daughter to Yan; Hulu's elder brother's son Buluzhen said to Hulu, "A young girl sent far in marriage will brood with sorrow—please take the daughters of ministers such as Shuli as accompanying brides."
translations.idiomatic: Rouran Khagan Hulu was about to marry his daughter to Yan; Buluzhen, a nephew of Hulu, said to him, "A young girl sent far in marriage will brood with sorrow—please take the daughters of ministers such as Shuli as accompanying brides."

sentences.zh: 斛律不許。

translations.literal: Hulu would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu refused.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真出，謂樹黎等曰：「斛律欲以汝女為媵，遠適他國。」

translations.literal: Buluzhen went out and said to Shuli and the others, "Hulu wishes to make your daughters accompanying brides and send them far to marry in another state."
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen went out and said to Shuli and the others, "Hulu wishes to make your daughters accompanying brides and marry them off to a distant land."

sentences.zh: 樹黎恐，與步鹿真謀使勇士夜伏於斛律穹廬之後，伺其出而執之，與女皆送於燕，立步鹿真為可汗而相之。

translations.literal: Shuli feared this; he and Buluzhen plotted to have brave men lie in ambush at night behind Hulu's yurt, wait for him to come out and seize him, and send him and the girl both to Yan; they installed Buluzhen as khagan and Shuli served as his chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Shuli was alarmed; he and Buluzhen plotted to have warriors lie in wait at night behind Hulu's yurt, seize him when he came out, and send him and the girl to Yan; they made Buluzhen khagan and Shuli served as his chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，社侖之徙高車也，高車人叱洛侯為之鄉導以並諸部，社侖德之，以為大人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shelun resettled the Gaoche, the Gaoche man Chiluohou had served as their guide in merging the tribes; Shelun rewarded him and made him a great chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shelun resettled the Gaoche, the Gaoche man Chiluohou had guided them in merging the tribes; Shelun was grateful and made him a great chieftain.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真與社侖之子社拔共至叱洛侯家，淫其少妻，妻告步鹿真曰：「叱洛侯欲奉大檀為主。」

translations.literal: Buluzhen and Shelun's son Sheba together went to Chiluohou's house and violated his young wife; the wife told Buluzhen, "Chiluohou intends to install Datan as ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen and Shelun's son Sheba went together to Chiluohou's house and violated his young wife; she told Buluzhen, "Chiluohou plans to install Datan as ruler."

sentences.zh: 大檀者，社侖季父僕渾之子也，領別部鎮西境，素得眾心。

translations.literal: Datan was the son of Shelun's uncle's son Puhun; he commanded a separate tribe guarding the western frontier and had long won the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Datan was the son of Puhun, Shelun's uncle's son; he commanded a separate tribe guarding the western frontier and had long enjoyed the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 步鹿真歸而發兵圍叱洛侯，叱洛侯自殺。

translations.literal: Buluzhen returned and raised troops to besiege Chiluohou; Chiluohou killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Buluzhen returned, raised troops, and besieged Chiluohou, who then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 遂引兵襲大檀，大檀逆擊，破之，執步鹿真及社拔，殺之，自立為可汗，號牟汗紇升蓋可汗。

translations.literal: He then led troops to attack Datan; Datan met the attack, defeated him, seized Buluzhen and Sheba, killed them, installed himself as khagan, and styled himself Khagan Mouhan Heshenggai.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops against Datan; Datan counterattacked, routed him, captured Buluzhen and Sheba and killed them, made himself khagan, and styled himself Khagan Mouhan Heshenggai.

sentences.zh: 斛律至和龍，燕王跋賜斛律爵上谷侯，館之遼東，待以客禮，納其女為昭儀。

translations.literal: Hulu reached Helong; King Ba of Yan enfeoffed Hulu as Marquis of Shanggu, lodged him in Liaodong, treated him with guest rites, and took his daughter as a Lady of Handsome Fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu arrived at Helong; King Ba of Yan enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shanggu, housed him in Liaodong, treated him as an honored guest, and took his daughter as a Lady of Handsome Fairness.

sentences.zh: 斛律上書請還其國，跋曰：「今度國萬里，又無內應，若以重兵相送，則饋運難繼。

translations.literal: Hulu memorialized asking to return to his state; Ba said, "Your state is now ten thousand li away, and there is no support within it; if we send you with a large force, supplies will be hard to sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu submitted a memorial asking to return home; Ba said, "Your country is ten thousand li away now, with no allies inside; if we escort you with a large army, supplies will be impossible to keep up.

sentences.zh: 兵少則不足成功，如何可還？」

translations.literal: With too few troops success would be impossible—how could you return?"
translations.idiomatic: Too few troops would not suffice for success—how could you go back?"

sentences.zh: 斛律固請，曰：「不煩重兵，願給三百騎，送至敕勒。

translations.literal: Hulu pressed his request, saying, "Without troubling you for a large force—I ask only for three hundred horsemen to escort me as far as the Chile.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu pressed his request, saying, "Do not trouble yourself with a large force—I ask only for three hundred horsemen to escort me to the Chile.

sentences.zh: 國人必欣然來迎。」

translations.literal: Our countrymen will surely come to welcome us with delight."
translations.idiomatic: Our people will surely come out gladly to meet us."

sentences.zh: 跋乃遣單于前輔萬陵帥騎三百送之。

translations.literal: Ba then sent the Former Chanyu Fu Wanling to lead three hundred horsemen to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Ba then sent the Former Chanyu Fu Wanling at the head of three hundred horsemen to escort him.

sentences.zh: 陵憚遠役，至黑山，殺斛律而還。

translations.literal: Wanling feared the distant service; reaching Black Mountain, he killed Hulu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wanling dreaded the long expedition; at Black Mountain he killed Hulu and turned back.

sentences.zh: 大檀亦遣使獻馬三千匹、羊萬口於燕。

translations.literal: Datan also sent envoys to present three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Datan also sent envoys to Yan with three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 六月，泰山太守劉研等帥流民七千餘家，河西胡酋劉遮等帥部落萬餘家，皆降於魏。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Taishan Administrator Liu Yan and others led more than seven thousand refugee households, and Hexi Hu chieftain Liu Zhe and others led more than ten thousand tribal households—all submitted to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Taishan Administrator Liu Yan and others led more than seven thousand refugee households, and Hexi Hu chieftain Liu Zhe and others led more than ten thousand tribal households; all surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏主嗣如豺山宮；

translations.literal: On wushen, Emperor Si of Wei went to Mount Chai Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Emperor Si of Wei went to Mount Chai Palace;

sentences.zh: 丁亥，還平城。

translations.literal: On dinghai, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 樂都之潰也，南涼安西將軍樊尼自西平奔告南涼王辱檀，辱檀謂其眾曰：「今妻子皆為熾磐所虜，退無所歸，卿等能與吾籍乙弗之資，取契汗以贖妻子乎？」

translations.literal: When Ledu fell, Southern Liang General Who Pacifies the West Fani fled from Xiping to report to Southern Liang King Rutan; Rutan said to his followers, "Our wives and children have all been captured by Chibpan; we have nowhere to retreat—can you join me in relying on Yifu's resources to take Qihan and ransom our wives and children?"
translations.idiomatic: When Ledu fell, Southern Liang General Who Pacifies the West Fani fled from Xiping to tell Southern Liang King Rutan; Rutan said to his men, "Our wives and children have all been taken by Chibpan; we have nowhere to fall back—will you join me in using Yifu's resources to seize Qihan and ransom our families?"

sentences.zh: 乃引兵西。

translations.literal: He then led his army west.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched west.

sentences.zh: 眾多逃還，辱檀遣鎮北將軍段苟追之，苟亦不還。

translations.literal: Many fled back; Rutan sent General Who Guards the North Duan Gou in pursuit, but Gou also did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Many men fled back; Rutan sent General Who Guards the North Duan Gou after them, but Gou never returned either.

sentences.zh: 於是將士皆散，唯樊尼與中軍將軍紇勃、後軍將軍洛肱、散騎侍郎陰利鹿不去。

translations.literal: At this the officers and soldiers all scattered; only Fani, General of the Central Army Hebo, General of the Rear Army Luogong, and Attendant Gentleman Yin Lilu did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Then the officers and soldiers all dispersed; only Fani, Central Army General Hebo, Rear Army General Luogong, and Attendant Gentleman Yin Lilu stayed.

sentences.zh: 辱檀曰：「蒙遜、熾磐昔皆委質於吾，今而歸之，不亦鄙乎！

translations.literal: Rutan said, "Mengxun and Chibpan both once pledged themselves to me—yet now you would go over to them; is that not base!
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said, "Mengxun and Chibpan both once pledged themselves to me—yet now you would go over to them; is that not shameful!

sentences.zh: 四海之廣，無所容身，何其痛也！

translations.literal: In all the wide world there is no place to shelter us—how bitter this is!
translations.idiomatic: In all the wide world there is no place for us—how painful this is!

sentences.zh: 與其聚而同死，不若分而或全。

translations.literal: Better to divide and perhaps survive than to gather and die together.
translations.idiomatic: Better to split up and perhaps survive than to stay together and die.

sentences.zh: 樊尼，吾長兄之子，宗部所寄；

translations.literal: Fani, my elder brother's son, is the hope of our clan;
translations.idiomatic: Fani, my elder brother's son, is the hope of our clan;

sentences.zh: 吾眾在北者戶垂一萬，蒙遜方招懷士民，存亡繼絕，汝其從之；
